items.title: Nigeria : les familles des victimes du crash militaire réclament des réponses, les enquêtes se multiplient
items.description: Les proches des victimes du crash d'un avion de l'armee de l'air nigeriane (NAF) denoncent le manque d'informations sur les circonstances de l'accident et la recuperation des depouilles. Le 5 octobre, un ATR-42 militaire reliant Benin City a Lagos s'etait ecrase dans une zone marecageuse d'Igbokoda, dans l'etat d'Ondo, faisant 25 morts, dont 19 militaires et six civils. Plusieurs familles endeuillees affirment n'avoir recu que peu d'informations des autorites. Le frere d'une militaire decedee dans le crash raconte que sa sœur avait envisage de poursuivre son trajet en bus apres un arret de l'appareil a Benin City, qu'elle attribuait a un probleme technique. Une autre famille affirme n'avoir ete contactee par aucun representant de l'armee. De son cote, la NAF assure poursuivre les recherches et s'engage a soutenir les proches des victimes. Des enquetes sur les causes du crash et l'entretien des avions Le president Bola Tinubu a ordonne une enquete sur l'accident. L'armee de l'air a mis en place une commission de douze membres chargee d'examiner les circonstances du crash, notamment les facteurs techniques, humains et organisationnels. Elle souligne qu'aucune conclusion ne peut etre tiree avant la fin des investigations. Le Senat et la Chambre des representants ont egalement decide d'enqueter sur l'entretien de la flotte militaire. Les parlementaires demandent un audit des appareils, un examen des budgets de maintenance et davantage de moyens pour remplacer les avions vieillissants. Le Senat reclame aussi la publication des conclusions de l'enquete. Ces investigations interviennent apres une serie d'accidents impliquant l'aviation militaire nigeriane. Au moins neuf accidents d'appareils de la NAF avaient fait plus de 30 morts au cours des cinq annees precedant cette catastrophe. Des inquietudes sanitaires a Igbokoda Sur les lieux du crash, les habitants redoutent les consequences environnementales de l'accident. Le chef d'Igbokoda, Afolabi Odidiomo, signale des odeurs nauseabondes, des restes humains flottant dans l'eau et des traces de carburant pres de l'epave. Il demande aux autorites d'accelerer la recuperation des depouilles, de nettoyer la zone et de fournir de l'eau potable a la population. Le commissaire a l'Environnement de l'etat d'Ondo, Tob Loko, reconnaît l'existence d'une pollution et indique qu'une evaluation des risques sanitaires est en cours. Il precise toutefois que les habitants disposent de forages et conteste les affirmations selon lesquelles ils seraient prives d'eau potable.

items.title: Missing $12.4bn: ADC asks Tinubu to explain Nigeria’s unaccounted funds
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain a $12.4 billion discrepancy in Nigeria’s external accounts identified by the World Bank, saying the amount is equivalent to nearly a quarter of the country’s N68.32 trillion 2026 federal budget. The party said the discrepancy demands urgent answers, especially as Nigerians battling rising living costs are forced to account for every naira while the government faces questions over the country’s foreign earnings. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC said Tinubu must account for the gap and disclose how oil export earnings and other foreign inflows are being managed. According to the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update, the country recorded a $12 billion current-account surplus and $6.2 billion in net financial inflows in the first half of the year. The report, however, identified a $12.4 billion gap in Nigeria’s external accounts. The World Bank attributed part of the discrepancy to oil export earnings that were not repatriated, noting that the return of export proceeds remained limited, partly because Nigerian crude had been pledged against several long-term loans. The ADC said the scale of the discrepancy made a detailed public explanation imperative. “The scale is staggering. This unexplained gap is larger than the entire current-account surplus for the same period. It is about 5.6 times the $2.2 billion Nigeria attracted in foreign direct investment. In naira terms, it is almost a quarter of the N68.32 trillion 2026 federal budget,” the party said. It accused Tinubu of celebrating the positive aspects of the World Bank report while failing to address the financial discrepancy it identified. “This cannot be dismissed as a minor accounting discrepancy. President Tinubu welcomed this report. He cannot celebrate one part of the report and stay silent on a gap bigger than the surplus that he and his government are celebrating,” the ADC said. The party also linked the issue to the economic hardship facing households, arguing that Nigerians should not be made to bear the burden of economic reforms without corresponding transparency from the government. “Due to President Tinubu’s failed policies, families across Nigeria are forced to skip meals and account for every naira just to survive. Meanwhile, money that could have been used to ease their hardship is currently unaccounted for. Tinubu owes Nigerians an explanation,” it said. “Sacrifice cannot be compulsory for everyday citizens while accountability remains optional for the government that is in charge of our collective resources,” the party added. The ADC demanded that the Federal Government publish a full reconciliation of the $12.4 billion discrepancy and disclose all oil-backed loans and pledged crude commitments. It also sought updated net reserve figures and evidence of how higher revenues were improving healthcare, education and electricity supply. “President Tinubu must open the books. Nigerians have sacrificed enough. We deserve answers,” the party said. The post Missing $12.4bn: ADC asks Tinubu to explain Nigeria’s unaccounted funds appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: World Food Day 2026: Forikrom women champion local foods and call for stronger support for rural farmers
items.description: As the world marks World Food Day under the theme “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow”, women farmers in Forikrom, in the Bono East Region, have added their voices to the global call for action, urging Ghanaians to eat local, support rural farmers, and push for policies that strengthen food security. The international day, an initiative of the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), comes amid growing pressure on global agrifood systems, with over 36 million people in West and Central Africa still struggling to access sufficient food. In Forikrom, the day was marked by a mini local food Durbar at the training camp of the Abrono Organic Farming Project (ABOFAP), organised in collaboration with the Rural Women Farmers Association of Ghana (RUWFAG). The event brought together women farmers, agricultural extension officers, nutrition experts, and traditional leaders to celebrate Ghana’s local foods and advocate for sustainable farming. Executive Director of ABOFAP, Nana Kwao Adams, encouraged participants to prioritise locally produced food and to work harder to produce enough food for the country. “We should eat our own food and keep working harder to produce the needed food for the country. It is time we look at policies that will empower rural farmers so that farming becomes sustainable,” he said. Chairing the function, Forikromhemaa Nana Sakyiwaa Abanaba, admonished Ghanaians to embrace the consumption of organic foods, which she described as healthy and beneficial. “I urge everyone to consume organic foods. They are healthy for our bodies and good for our well-being,” she stated. Anita Suntaa, National Coordinator for the Rural Women Farmers Association of Ghana, called for policies that will help women farmers produce enough food. “We need policies that will help women farmers produce enough food. This includes the establishment of irrigation systems to aid all-year-round farming, particularly in the Upper West Region,” she said. Festus Addai, the Techiman Municipal Agric Extension Officer, noted that despite available resources to produce more food, it is quite unfortunate that many people still go hungry. “With available resources to produce more food, it’s quite unfortunate that a lot of people still go hungry. More needs to be done to address this,” he emphasised. Faiza Issah, Nutrition Officer at the Forikrom Health Centre, admonished participants to consume local foods that contain the four-star diet—a nutrition framework promoting a balanced intake of different food groups for good health. “I admonish us all to consume our local foods that contain the four-star diet for our good health,” she advised. This year’s World Food Day commemoration in Forikrom served as a reminder that sustainable food systems begin with supporting those who produce our food—especially rural women farmers—and with a collective commitment to eating what we grow. As the world reflects on the challenges facing global agrifood systems, the message from Forikrom is clear: empower rural farmers, invest in irrigation, promote organic and local foods, and ensure that no one goes hungry.

items.title: Fanaka International University & GISI sign MoU to enhance professional capital market training
items.description: Fanaka International University College and the Ghana Investment and Securities Institute (GISI) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to integrate professional capital market training into Fanaka’s Master of Science in Finance programme. The partnership is expected to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry practice, while equipping students with the skills and professional qualifications needed to pursue careers in the securities and investment industry. The collaboration between Fanaka International University College and the Ghana Investment and Securities Institute will strengthen professional standards and build capacity within Ghana’s capital market. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Rector of Fanaka International University College, Professor Samuel Agyei-Ampomah, said the collaboration will help enhance knowledge of students in finance and investment. “The financial curriculum landscape is shifting rapidly, and with GISI’s leadership and continuous professional development, students and faculty will have direct access to cutting-edge insights on modern asset classes, corporate governance and digital financial frameworks”, he said. Through the collaboration, students will benefit from practical industry exposure and professional development opportunities that could improve their readiness for employment in securities trading, investment management and other areas of the financial services industry. Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment and Securities Institute, Alexander Williams, said the collaboration would promote curriculum benchmarking, professional development and closer engagement between academia and industry. The agreement also reflects broader efforts to strengthen the relationship between universities and professional institutions, ensuring that graduates leave school with knowledge that responds to the needs of the job market. For Ghana’s capital market, the collaboration is expected to contribute to the development of a pipeline of skilled professionals who can support investment activities, improve market participation and contribute to the growth of the country’s financial sector. The partnership is expected to provide students with practical industry exposure and internationally recognised professional development opportunities, while strengthening the pipeline of skilled professionals for Ghana’s securities and investment market.

items.title: Médias : le Premier ministre à l’écoute des préoccupations du secteur
items.description: Le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô a présidé, vendredi 16 octobre 2026, au Building administratif Président Mamadou Dia, une séance de travail avec les acteurs des médias. Les échanges ont porté sur les difficultés économiques des entreprises de presse, les conditions de travail des professionnels, la régulation du secteur et l’avenir des médias publics et communautaires. Le Gouvernement a réaffirmé sa volonté d’accompagner durablement la profession. Les acteurs des médias ont exposé leurs préoccupations au chef du Gouvernement. Cette rencontre, à laquelle a pris part le ministre de la Communication et des Relations avec les institutions, porte-parole du Gouvernement, Dr Bacary Sarr, a réuni les organisations professionnelles, les responsables des médias publics et parapublics ainsi que plusieurs structures chargées de l’encadrement du secteur. Les discussions ont d’abord mis en lumière les difficultés économiques, structurelles et fiscales auxquelles les entreprises de presse sont confrontées. Le Conseil des diffuseurs et éditeurs de presse du Sénégal (CDEPS) a porté ces préoccupations, dans un contexte où la viabilité économique des médias constitue un enjeu majeur pour la pérennité de leurs activités. La situation des journalistes et des techniciens a également occupé une place importante dans les échanges. Le Syndicat des professionnels de l’information et de la communication du Sénégal (SYNPICS) et la Convention des jeunes reporters du Sénégal (CJRS) ont évoqué les conditions de travail des professionnels de l’information. Régulation et conditions d’exercice au cœur des échanges La rencontre a aussi permis d’aborder les questions d’éthique, de déontologie et de régulation. Le Conseil pour l’observation des règles d’éthique et de déontologie dans les médias (CORED), la Commission de la carte nationale de presse (CNCP) et les experts présents ont apporté leurs éclairages sur les mécanismes d’encadrement de la profession et les enjeux liés à son assainissement. Les radios associatives et communautaires, représentées par l’Union des radios associatives et communautaires (URAC), ont, pour leur part, présenté les défis et les perspectives de ce segment du paysage médiatique. Les responsables des structures publiques et parapubliques ont également pris la parole. La Radiotélévision sénégalaise (RTS), la Société sénégalaise de presse et de publications Le Soleil, l’Agence de presse sénégalaise (APS) et Télédiffusion du Sénégal (TDS-SA) ont exposé leurs contraintes opérationnelles et apporté des contributions techniques aux discussions. Autre point abordé : la mise en place du Conseil national de régulation des médias (CNRM), appelé à remplacer le Conseil national de régulation de l’audiovisuel (CNRA). Le Bureau organisation et méthodes (BOM) a fait le point sur l’état d’avancement du processus de recrutement des membres de la nouvelle instance. Le Gouvernement promet un accompagnement durable Au terme des interventions, le Premier ministre, aux côtés du ministre de la Communication, a apporté des réponses aux préoccupations soulevées par les participants. Selon le compte rendu de la rencontre, ces échanges traduisent la volonté du Gouvernement d’accompagner le secteur dans ses efforts de modernisation et de stabilisation économique. Cette concertation intervient alors que les entreprises de presse, les professionnels de l’information et les organes de régulation sont confrontés à des défis qui touchent aussi bien à la viabilité des médias qu’aux conditions d’exercice du métier et au respect des règles déontologiques. Le Gouvernement entend ainsi poursuivre le dialogue avec les acteurs du secteur autour de ces enjeux, avec pour objectif affiché de contribuer à la modernisation des médias et à la consolidation de l’État de droit.

items.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released from police custody
items.description: India’s Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was released from detention on Saturday, a day after he was detained during a police crackdown on protests against the election authority. Dipke, 31, was detained on Friday in New Delhi as he headed to join a rally that the CJP protest movement had called in the capital’s central Connaught Place district. He was arrested to prevent a breach of the peace, broadcasters NDTV and ​ India Today reported. He walked out of a police station on Saturday afternoon, waving to the media and giving a thumbs up as he was driven away, an AFP photographer saw. “Abhijeet Dipke released,” CJP legal affairs chief Ratna Singh said on social media. Opposition parties and CJP activists have defied a security crackdown , rallying to demand the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party. More than 130 million voters were deleted ​during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Student activist Neha ​Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she ​tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released earlier on Saturday as well. “Please, spare the people of India. ‌Impeach ⁠Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured,” Bora told ANI news agency after she was released. Two other senior CJP leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, were arrested on Oct 14 after entering Jantar Mantar , a decades-old protest site that police have declared off-limits for demonstrations. They remain in custody. Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls. Rights groups and critics, however, say Modi’s government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents — allegations the government rejects. A weeks-long sit-in by supporters of the movement earlier this year forced then-education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over ​exam paper leaks.

items.title: Secrétariat général de l’ONU : Ces possibles obstacles à l’élection de Macky Sall
items.description: L’annonce, ce samedi 17 octobre 2026, par Macky Sall de son retrait à la candidature du poste de secrétaire General de l’Organisation des Nations Unies (ONU) vient clore une séquence diplomatique. Cette dernière aura mobilisé des soutiens, réveillé des fractures et montré des obstacles. L’ancien Président du Sénégal, Macky Sall briguait légitiment la succession d’António Guterres, dont le mandat s’achève le 31 décembre 2026. Douze années à la tête de l’État sénégalais, une expérience des négociations internationales et un passage à la présidence en exercice de l’Union africaine constituaient des atouts. Macky Sall abordait donc cette séquence avec un parcours substantiel. Ancien ministre plusieurs fois, ancien Premier ministre, ancien président de l’Assemblée nationale, puis président de la République de 2012 à 2024, il a occupé pendant plus d’une décennie les plus hautes fonctions de l’État sénégalais. À la tête de l’Union africaine, Macky Sall a été associé aux discussions sur la représentation du continent dans les institutions internationales. Il s’est beaucoup impliqué sur des questions concernant la dette des pays en développement, le financement de l’action climatique et les conséquences économiques de la guerre en Ukraine. Dans son document de candidature, intitulé «Refonder le multilatéralisme pour un monde meilleur», Macky Sall plaide pour une organisation plus efficace, plus moderne et mieux adaptée aux crises contemporaines. Il met notamment en avant les conflits persistants, l’endettement des pays en développement et l’affaiblissement de la confiance dans les institutions internationales. Toutefois, une candidature au secrétariat général de l’ONU suppose de réunir des soutiens diplomatiques suffisamment larges. Dans cet ordre, l’enjeu le plus capital est sans doute de rassurer les puissances déterminantes (USA, France Chine, Russie, Royaumes Unis). Un candidat africain, sans consensus africain L’un des premiers obstacles aura été la difficulté à présenter la candidature de Macky Sall comme l’expression d’une volonté africaine unifiée. Le Burundi, alors à la tête de la présidence tournante de l’Union africaine, a parrainé la candidature de l’ancien président sénégalais. Ce soutien constituait un point d’appui important. Mais l’ensemble des gouvernements africains n’a pas suit. La succession d’António Guterres s’inscrit également dans un contexte où l’Amérique latine et les Caraïbes sont appelées à être privilégiée dans la logique de rotation géographique. Cette pratique n’est pas une règle juridique contraignante, mais elle pèse sur les équilibres diplomatiques. La perspective de voir une femme accéder pour la première fois au secrétariat général constitue également un élément important. La candidature de Macky Sall devait donc surmonter des considérations régionales et symboliques qui dépassent sa personne. Le Conseil de sécurité, ultime juge Le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, lors du vote indicatif organisé dans le cadre de la sélection du successeur d’António Guterres, Macky Sall a obtenu cinq avis favorables contre dix défavorables. Trois des avis négatifs provenaient de membres permanents du Conseil, selon les résultats rapportés par la presse. Ces consultations informelles ne constituent pas un scrutin éliminatoire. Elles servent néanmoins à mesurer les rapports de force avant la procédure formelle. Le mécanisme de désignation du secrétaire général confère un poids décisif aux cinq membres permanents. Le retrait, une décision lucide Le samedi 17 octobre, Macky Sall a annoncé son retrait après des consultations avec le président Burundais Évariste Ndayishimiye, président en exercice de l’Union africaine, et le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, également président en exercice de la CEDEAO. Dans sa déclaration, l’ancien chef de l’État explique que les différents votes tests traduisaient une préférence pour une candidature issue de l’Amérique latine et des Caraïbes, éventuellement féminine. Il a indiqué vouloir favoriser l’émergence d’une candidature consensuelle. Pour Macky Sall, l’ambition Onusienne s’achève. Cette séquence met toutefois en lumière les limites d’une ambition internationale, lorsqu’elle ne parvient pas à mobiliser, des soutiens suffisamment solides. O.BA

items.title: Smiling pope returns to Vatican after cancer surgery
items.description: Pope Leo XIV left the hospital to enthusiastic cheers and applause from well-wishers and returned home to the Vatican on Saturday, four days after undergoing surgery for lung cancer. The 71-year-old pope was seen crossing the lobby of the Gemelli Hospital on foot and exiting the building, smiling as he shook hands and waved. He spoke briefly to the doctors who treated him and hospital officials before pausing to speak with a Ukrainian girl, a cancer survivor who wanted to wish him well in his recovery. Soon after leaving the hospital, the pope’s black SUV was seen driving through a side entrance to the Vatican. Leo’s discharge capped five days of uncertainty that rattled the Vatican and the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, less than two years into the Chicago-born pope’s papacy, which began upon his election on May 8 last year. Earlier on Saturday, Leo’s doctors said the pope was “ fit for discharge”, according to the Vatican. He had been at the Gemelli Hospital north of the Vatican since Tuesday when doctors removed part of his right lung to extract a cancerous tumour. “Considering the blood tests, the chest X-ray done this morning, and evaluating the clinical picture, the Holy Father has been deemed fit for discharge,” doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora wrote in a note published by the Vatican. This photo taken and handout on October 17, 2026 by The Vatican Media shows Pope Leo XIV shaking hands with his surgeon Stefano Margaritora outside the Gemelli University Hospital in Rome, Italy before leaving four days after a surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung. — AFP The Vatican said that Leo on Sunday planned to recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St Peter’s Square, as is customary. Before his discharge, Leo celebrated Mass at noon, according to the Vatican, as he has in recent days, in a room on the 10th floor where he has been recovering. The 13-year-old Ukrainian girl who spoke with the pope outside the hospital earlier on Saturday told AFP that she was rooting for him. The cancer survivor said she had met the pope last year in Rome, “and he blessed me for a successful treatment”. “With his support, I’ve now overcome my illness, and I want to give him my positive energy so that he, too, can overcome his illness as quickly as possible,” she said. Up in the air News that the otherwise active pope had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung was met with trepidation among the world’s Catholics and other supporters. But his doctors have said Leo’s recovery has been progressing normally as they await the results of tests that will determine the course of action to take. Leo has resumed some work, making a call on Friday to Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky. Up in the air, however, is a planned papal voyage to South America, scheduled for November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Vatican watchers say that Leo — who spent two decades as a missionary in Peru — is anxious to make the long journey, but will likely follow the recommendations of his doctors. Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20. The pope announced to the public in St Peter’s Square last Sunday, following the Angelus prayer, that a routine medical examination had revealed a nodule that doctors recommended should be removed.

items.title: Diana Hamilton releases new single ‘Wate M’anim’
items.description: Diana Hamilton has released her new single, “Wate M’anim,” which arrived on Friday, 16 October 2026, across all streaming platforms, alongside its accompanying music video on YouTube. Written by Cofi Boham and produced by Herbert Crassie (Oshogbo), the song presents a testimony of gratitude, reflecting on God’s faithfulness and the journey that has shaped Diana’s life and ministry. Meaning “You Have Honoured Me,” “W’ate M’anim” draws attention to the grace behind the journey. Its message encourages listeners to pause, look back, and recognise God’s hand in their own stories, while embracing the future with faith. For the accompanying video, Diana once again partners with McWillies, continuing a creative relationship that includes work on some of her award-winning videos, such as “Adom” and “Mo ne yo.” Their renewed collaboration brings a personal testimony to the screen through artistic storytelling. The video offers a glimpse into Diana’s past while using imagery to look towards the future. Moving between remembrance and expectation, it connects where she has come from with the hope she carries for what lies ahead. This retrospective approach gives audiences an opportunity to reflect on the person and the journey behind the music. The past becomes part of a continuing testimony, while the imagery of the future expresses anticipation for the next chapter. For those who have followed Diana’s ministry over the years, “Wate M’anim” offers a moment of shared reflection and thanksgiving. For new listeners, it provides an invitation to connect with a message that reaches beyond one person’s experience: every life carries a story, and every testimony can become a source of encouragement to someone else. As Diana looks back with gratitude and forward with expectation, “W’ate M’anim” invites audiences to do the same, to remember, give thanks, and keep trusting God for the journey ahead. Stream “W’ate Manim” now on all streaming platforms and watch the accompanying music video on Diana Hamilton’s YouTube channel.

items.title: Ghana proposes visa waiver agreement with Lebanon to boost bilateral ties
items.description: Ghana has proposed a visa waiver agreement with Lebanon covering holders of diplomatic, service, and ordinary passports to strengthen bilateral relations and facilitate travel, trade, and investment between the two countries. Ghana’s Ambassador to the Republic of Lebanon, with residence in Cairo, Egypt, H.E. Prof. Justice Solomon Korantwi-Barimah, highlighted the proposal during the presentation of his Letters of Credence to Lebanese President H.E. Joseph Aoun in Beirut on Thursday, October 15, 2026. The proposed agreement is expected to promote people-to-people exchanges, facilitate business engagements and reinforce the longstanding friendship between Ghana and Lebanon. Prof. Korantwi-Barimah reaffirmed Ghana’s readiness to work with the Lebanese government to identify new areas of cooperation and advance shared interests. Strengthening longstanding relations The Ambassador conveyed greetings from President John Dramani Mahama, the Government and people of Ghana to President Aoun and the people of Lebanon. He underscored Ghana’s commitment to deepening relations with Lebanon, noting that the two countries established formal diplomatic ties in the early years of Ghana’s independence in 1957. Lebanon, he said, was the second country in the Middle East with which Ghana established formal diplomatic relations. He added that the relationship predated formal diplomatic engagement and had grown over the years through commercial exchanges, people-to-people interactions and the settlement of Lebanese nationals in Ghana. Prof. Korantwi-Barimah acknowledged the contributions of the Lebanese community to Ghana’s social and economic development, describing its integration into Ghanaian society as evidence of the enduring friendship and mutual trust between the two countries. Trade and investment opportunities On economic cooperation, the Ambassador commended Lebanese businesses for their longstanding investments in Ghana and their contributions to the country’s development. He expressed Ghana’s interest in expanding collaboration with Lebanon in trade, investment, hospitality, education, healthcare and tourism. According to him, stronger partnerships in these sectors could open up investment opportunities, encourage knowledge and skills transfer, create jobs and support sustainable economic growth in both countries. He reiterated Ghana’s willingness to engage the Lebanese government and private sector to translate the longstanding relationship into practical economic benefits. Cooperation on international issues Prof. Korantwi-Barimah also expressed Ghana’s appreciation for Lebanon’s support for the adoption of United Nations General Assembly Resolution A/RES/80/250, concerning the trafficking of enslaved Africans and the racialised chattel enslavement of Africans as the gravest crime against humanity. He described Lebanon’s support as a demonstration of international solidarity and recognition of the importance of historical truth, justice and human dignity. The Ambassador further highlighted Ghana’s longstanding contribution to the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), noting that the country’s participation reflected its commitment to international peace and security. He reaffirmed Ghana’s support for peaceful conflict resolution and diplomatic initiatives aimed at promoting dialogue, stability and security at the regional and international levels. He also expressed interest in strengthening cooperation with Lebanon on issues of mutual concern, including sustainable development and relations between Africa and the Middle East. Labour and migration On labour and migration, the Ambassador welcomed discussions between the two governments on establishing appropriate frameworks to manage labour mobility and migration. He said closer cooperation could promote orderly migration, strengthen institutional collaboration and improve workers’ welfare and protection in line with applicable national laws and international obligations. Prof. Korantwi-Barimah expressed Ghana’s readiness to engage relevant Lebanese authorities to explore practical arrangements that address the concerns of both countries. Commitment to deeper cooperation The Ambassador reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to working with the Lebanese government and relevant institutions to strengthen cooperation at both bilateral and multilateral levels. He expressed confidence that sustained dialogue and mutual understanding would create further opportunities for collaboration and deepen the longstanding friendship between the two countries. He also thanked President Aoun for the warm reception accorded to him and his delegation, expressing optimism about a productive tenure focused on advancing the shared interests of Ghana and Lebanon.

items.title: In-form Atletico snatch late win at Espanyol
items.description: Alex Baena struck in the 89th minute to snatch Atletico Madrid a 1-0 win at Espanyol and put pressure on La Liga leaders Barcelona on Saturday. Diego Simeone’s side, second, moved two points behind Hansi Flick’s champions, who visit third-placed Real Betis later on. Spain international Baena smashed home from the edge of the box to claim the Rojiblancos an important late victory from a tight game in Cornella. Atletico have won six consecutive games across all competitions. “They had a good game defensively and it was hard for us,” Baena told DAZN. “The good thing this team has is that it keeps believing until the 90th minute.” Baena, who struggled last season but has been in fine fettle since winning the World Cup with Spain this summer, hugged coach Simeone after finding the net. “He’s a player who can do a lot of damage, who is in very good form,” Simeone told DAZN after Baena’s fifth league goal of the season. Both sides had chances in the first half but Espanyol came closest as Leandro Cabrera struck the crossbar. Marcos Llorente hit the same woodwork after an hour with a long-range effort for Atletico. Espanyol brought on captain Javi Puado after a long-term knee injury, as he made his first appearance since January. Julian Alvarez was bright for Atletico as a substitute as he continues to find his form after trying to force a move away in the summer. Atletico have left it late several times this season to claim points and did so again here, with Baena thumping home from Alvarez’s pass to earn his team’s victory. “Last year (Baena) started well but then injuries prevented him from reaching his best form and having the season he wanted,” Simeone told reporters. “The World Cup took him to a different place, he sees football differently than others and (now) he’s more confident and stronger, he’s the player we went looking for.” Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak made a good save in stoppage time from Pol Lozano to ensure his team kept the three points. On Sunday Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla among other fixtures. AFP The post In-form Atletico snatch late win at Espanyol appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Disqualify Obuasi SHTS headmaster from Juaben NDC chairmanship race – Former NDC MP urges party
items.description: Former National Democratic Congress (NDC) Member of Parliament for Amenfi Central, Peter Kwakye Ackah, has called on the party to disqualify the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, from contesting the party’s upcoming constituency election, saying his candidacy would be a disgrace to the party. Mr Abdulai, who is accused of sexually abusing about 16 students at the school, is contesting the chairmanship of the NDC in the Juaben constituency. Speaking on Adom TV’s Nnawɔtwe Yi on Saturday, October 17, Mr Ackah said party membership should not protect him. “Nobody should shield such a person after he has raped someone’s child just because he’s a party member,” Mr Ackah said. The Ghana Education Service (GES) has interdicted Mr Abdulai following a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni, and a complaint has been lodged with the police. Mr Ackah urged the constituency vetting committee to bar Zakaria from the race. “I am appealing to the constituency vetting committee not to allow such a person to lead the party; he will collapse the party.” He also asked the party’s national leadership to ensure that Mr Abdulai is suspended from the NDC, adding that there was no justification for what the headmaster is alleged to have done. The former MP said suspension alone is not enough and called on the President, the Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, and the Interior Minister, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, to get involved. “I’m appealing to the President to take it up and give the order to the Minister. Haruna, you must not sit on this at all.” Mr Ackah also faulted the Obuasi Municipal Chief Executive, saying she failed to handle the matter properly after one victim’s family approached her. “The girl is even ashamed to come out, so since her parents have come to you, why didn’t you take action… what is happening?” he questioned. He said the student unrest that brought the case to public attention was not wrong, arguing that the students took matters into their own hands because they saw that the law was not working. Such actions, he warned, will become the order of the day if the law keeps failing. The GES has said the unrest led to the destruction of school property and the temporary closure of the school.

items.description: Abdeljabbar Errachidi, que le Roi Mohammed VI a nommé, vendredi, ministre délégué auprès du ministre du Tourisme, de l’Artisanat et de l’Economie solidaire, chargé de l’Artisanat et de l’Economie solidaire, est né le 27 octobre 1968 à Tanger. Titulaire d'un doctorat en droit public de l'Université Hassan II de Mohammedia et d'un diplôme des études supérieures en information et communication de l'Institut supérieur de l’information et de la communication de Rabat, Errachidi a occupé le poste de Secrétaire d’État chargé de l’Insertion sociale, ainsi que de chef du pôle de la communication et de l’information au ministère délégué chargé des Affaires générales et de la Gouvernance. Membre élu du Conseil régional de Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima, il a également exercé en qualité de chargé d’études à la Primature, de chargé de mission auprès du ministre au sein du ministère des Affaires générales et économiques, et de conseiller du ministre au ministère chargé des Relations avec le Parlement. The post Abdeljabbar Errachidi, ministre délégué chargé de l’Artisanat et de l’Economie solidaire appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Jérôme Fourquet, sociólogo: “Estamos ante el final de un reinado en Francia”
items.description: Jérôme Fourquet (Le Mans, 53 años) no suele equivocarse. Y si lo hace, lo hace de forma elegante. El gurú demoscópico —es director de Opinión del instituto IFOP—, politólogo y ensayista, ha descifrado mejor que nadie el malestar creciente en la sociedad francesa. El clima de descomposición, las fracturas, las desigualdades que han alimentado los extremos. Ahora, en plena ola de protestas, cree que el país se encamina a un callejón sin salida. Un fin de reinado, como él mismo lo define por videoconferencia, que ni siquiera tiene garantizada una solución tras las próximas elecciones presidenciales. Seguir leyendo

‎Pacte NEKRE : un engagement collectif pour refonder l’école burkinabé
items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, représentant le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a présidé, ce samedi 17 octobre 2026 à Kaya, la cérémonie officielle de lancement du Pacte pour la refondation de l’école burkinabè, baptisé « Pacte NEKRE ». La rencontre a réuni des Présidents d'institutions, des membres du Gouvernement, des représentants du corps diplomatique et des acteurs du système éducatif autour d’une ambition commune : garantir à chaque enfant une éducation sûre, inclusive, souveraine et d’excellence. Le choix du 17 octobre inscrit cette initiative dans le prolongement de l’Appel de Gaoua, lancé quarante ans plus tôt, le 17 octobre 1986, par le Camarade Thomas Sankara. Cet appel à la qualité de l’enseignement et à la révolution des consciences rappelait la nécessité d’une école exigeante, portée par des enseignants engagés et une communauté mobilisée. Le Pacte NEKRE entend traduire cet héritage en engagements précis, partagés et assumés. ‎ Le choix de Kaya revêt également une double symbolique, soulignée dans le message du Président du Faso. Terre de solidarité, la ville a accueilli des familles déplacées, dont certaines regagnent progressivement leurs villages reconquis. Elle est aussi présentée comme le bastion d’où est parti le sursaut patriotique de la Révolution progressiste populaire. Elle incarne ainsi la résilience du peuple burkinabè et la volonté de faire de chaque territoire reconquis un espace de renaissance nationale. Dans son message livré par le Camarade Premier ministre, le Chef de l’État appelle à une transformation profonde de l’école, touchant aussi bien son organisation, ses programmes et sa gouvernance que la formation morale et civique des apprenants. L’objectif est de former des citoyens responsables, enracinés dans leurs valeurs, capables de produire, d’innover et de servir l’intérêt général. Pour concrétiser cette ambition, il fixe sept « ordres de marche » : ne laisser aucun enfant ou jeune en marge de l’éducation ; garantir des conditions d’apprentissage dignes ; rapprocher les savoirs de la production et des métiers ; valoriser les langues nationales, l’histoire et les savoirs endogènes ; renforcer la place de l’enseignant ; mettre la science, le numérique et la recherche au service de la souveraineté ; et instaurer une gouvernance fondée sur des données fiables et la reddition des comptes. ‎ L’accès à l’éducation occupe une place centrale dans cette démarche, notamment pour les enfants vulnérables, ceux qui n’ont jamais été scolarisés et ceux qui ont quitté l’école. « Là où l’État revient, l’école doit rouvrir ! », affirme le Président du Faso. Cette exigence s’accompagne de l’amélioration des infrastructures, de l’accès à l’eau, aux latrines et aux manuels, ainsi que des conditions de logement, d’alimentation et de santé des étudiants. ‎ Les apprentissages devront, pour leur part, associer des connaissances solides à des compétences pratiques et à la maîtrise progressive d’un métier. Les langues nationales et les savoirs endogènes sont appelés à devenir des instruments de connaissance, tandis que la recherche et l’innovation devront apporter des réponses concrètes aux besoins de l’agriculture, de la santé, de l’industrie et de l’environnement. ‎ La mise en œuvre de ces orientations repose sur une répartition claire des responsabilités. L’État doit assurer un financement équitable et soutenu, protéger les espaces éducatifs, améliorer les conditions d’enseignement et garantir le respect des normes. Le contrôle des établissements privés sera renforcé, notamment en matière de qualité de l’encadrement, de sécurité des apprenants et de respect des droits des personnels : contrats, paiement régulier des rémunérations et protection sociale. ‎ Cette responsabilité collective s’est exprimée, au cours de la cérémonie, par la lecture et la signature solennelles des déclarations d’engagement des représentants des enseignants, des élèves, des parents d’élèves ainsi que des acteurs et partenaires de l’école. ‎ Les enseignants se sont engagés à exercer leur métier avec compétence, conscience professionnelle, impartialité et dignité. Pour accompagner cet engagement, une charte nationale d’éthique et d’engagement professionnel sera élaborée avec les acteurs, puis adoptée au niveau national. Le message présidentiel affirme également la tolérance zéro à l’égard des pratiques contraires à l’éthique et annonce une réponse ferme de l’État aux violences contre les enseignants. ‎ Les élèves ont, quant à eux, promis de faire preuve d’assiduité, de discipline, d’honnêteté et de respect du bien commun. De leur côté, les parents d’élèves ont pris l’engagement de renforcer le suivi scolaire de leurs enfants, de leur transmettre les valeurs morales et de lutter contre les pratiques qui les détournent de l’école. Le renforcement des cadres de concertation entre parents et établissements doit soutenir cette complémentarité éducative et contribuer à prévenir le décrochage scolaire. ‎ ‎Les acteurs et partenaires de l’éducation ont également appelé à une mobilisation permanente et à des actions concrètes, mesurables et durables. Leaders communautaires, organisations de la société civile, entreprises et partenaires sociaux sont ainsi invités à contribuer à la protection des enfants, à la continuité des apprentissages et à l’insertion professionnelle des jeunes. ‎ ‎Pour donner une portée effective à ces engagements, le message présidentiel pose une exigence de suivi : chaque engagement devra avoir un responsable, chaque action une échéance et chaque ressource une destination clairement définie. Les résultats seront régulièrement évalués et les insuffisances corrigées. ‎ ‎Le Pacte NEKRE a ensuite été symboliquement remis aux gouverneurs de région, en vue de sa mise en œuvre sur l’ensemble du territoire national. ‎ ‎À travers cette initiative, le Burkina Faso fait de la refondation de l’école une responsabilité nationale partagée. Sa réussite reposera sur la capacité de chaque acteur à traduire ses engagements en actes, au service de l’enfant, de la souveraineté et de l’intérêt supérieur de la Nation. ‎ ‎𝐃𝐂𝐑𝐏/𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 ‎

items.title: ONU : Macky Sall retire sa candidature au poste de secrétaire général
items.description: L'ex président sénégalais, Macky Sall jusque-là candidat au poste de secrétaire général de l'organisation des nations unies (ONU), a annoncé, ce samedi 17 octobre 2026 à Marrakech au Maroc, le retrait de sa candidature à la tête de cette instance international. L'information a été rendue publique via sa page Facebook officielle à l'issue du vote informel du 16 octobre. Macky Sall, n'est candidat au posté du secrétaire général de l'ONU. L'homme a mis fin à sa propre course dans cette aventure internationale. Selon un communiqué apogeant sa signature, cette décision a été prise suite au vote informel du 16 octobre 2026, après consultations avec les présidents Général Evariste Ndayishimiye du Burundi, Président en exercice de l’Union Africaine, et sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, président en exercice de la CEDEAO. « J’ai décidé de retirer ma candidature audit poste (…) », a-t-il déclaré dans le communiqué. « J'ai pris cette décision avec un profond sens des responsabilités, en espérant contribuer ainsi à l'émergence d'une candidature consensuelle au sein du Conseil de sécurité; gardant à l'esprit que depuis le début du processus, les résultats des différents votes tests indiquent un choix en faveur d'une candidature issue de la région d'Amérique latine et des Caraïbes, et éventuellement féminine », a poursuivi Macky Sall. Pour sa part, sa candidature était essentiellement motivée par la volonté de mettre son expérience de près de quarante ans de vie publique au service des Nations Unies. Alors que le monde reste confronté à la multiplication des conflits, à l'aggravation des rivalités géopolitiques, à la fragmentation de l'ordre international et à des défis économiques et financiers sans précédent, Macky Sall avisé que l'Afrique, qui est au cœur des enjeux de paix, de sécurité et de développement, Macky Sall a estimé que l'Afrique doit aussi continuer à faire entendre sa voix et poursuivre ses efforts afin d'occuper la place qui lui revient dans la gouvernance mondiale. items.title: CDD-Ghana calls for Deputy EC Chair Affi Agbenyo’s resignation over affiliation concerns
items.description: The Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana) has called for the resignation of Electoral Commission (EC) Deputy Chairperson Emelia Afi Agbenyo over concerns about her alleged affiliation with the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC). The centre has urged President John Dramani Mahama to advise Mrs Agbenyo to step down, arguing that the concerns surrounding her appointment could undermine public confidence in the independence and impartiality of the Electoral Commission. CDD-Ghana’s Programmes Manager, Paul Aborampah Mensah, made the call during an interview on Friday, October 16. Mr Mensah said the President could advise Mrs Agbenyo to resign if he had not fully considered the implications of the appointment, adding that she could also step down on moral grounds. “What we are demanding now is that perhaps the President did not recognise the impact of the appointment he was making. Now that it has been realised publicly, he can advise the lady to resign, or the lady, on moral grounds, can herself resign,” he said on Citi FM. He stressed the need to protect the independence of state institutions, warning against a situation in which changes in government routinely affect the leadership and operations of key national institutions. “We don’t want a situation where after every change of government our institutions are affected. That’s what we need to avoid as a country,” he said. Mr Mensah further cautioned that the continued politicisation of electoral management could have serious consequences for Ghana’s democratic processes. “If we are not careful and continue that way, it will get to a point that we’ll be sorry for the kind of people who have been managing our elections,” he added. The call follows the swearing-in of Mrs Agbenyo and Dr Joseph Kweku Asamoah as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission by President Mahama on October 12. The appointments have generated debate over Mrs Agbenyo’s alleged affiliation with the NDC, with critics raising concerns about whether such associations could affect public confidence in the Commission’s ability to carry out its mandate impartially. At the swearing-in ceremony, President Mahama urged the newly appointed deputy chairpersons to uphold impartiality and safeguard the right of Ghanaians to freely choose their leaders.

Lawyers fault demand for deposits before emergency treatment of patients
items.description: Some Lagos-based lawyers on Saturday, warned hospitals and healthcare providers against demanding upfront payments before treating patients in medical emergencies. The lawyers told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) that such actions violate the National Health Act of 2014, and attract legal sanctions. They argue that section 20(1) of the Act prohibited healthcare providers, health workers and health establishments from refusing emergency medical treatment for any reason, including a patient’s inability to pay a deposit. The lawyers, however, called for effective healthcare financing and reimbursement mechanisms, to protect hospitals from financial losses while ensuring that patients received timely medical attention. An Associate of the Institute of Medical and Health Law, Ms Odinichionye Egwuenu, told NAN that the law was clear that emergency treatment must not be withheld because a patient could not make upfront payment. Egwuenu said the provision applied to both public and private hospitals, noting that internal hospital policies could not override statutory obligations. She, however, urged stakeholders to consider the financial challenges facing healthcare institutions, including staff salaries, equipment maintenance and the procurement of medications. According to her, the situation becomes more complicated when a hospital provides emergency treatment but the patient dies and the family subsequently abandons the deceased or refuses to settle the outstanding medical bills. “We must also consider the practical realities of healthcare delivery; Hospitals have staff to pay, equipment to maintain and medications to purchase. “So, while human life must take priority in an emergency, what happens when a hospital provides treatment, the patient dies despite its efforts, and the family abandons the deceased,” she said While noting that section 11 of the National Health Act established the Basic Health Care Provision Fund, she said that the effectiveness of such funding required clos examination to determine whether hospitals received adequate support for emergency services. Meanwhile, she also drew attention to the Compulsory Treatment and Care for Victims of Gunshot Act, 2017, which requires hospitals to treat gunshot victims without demanding deposits or insisting on police clearance. She urged hospitals to notify the nearest police station within two hours of commencing treatment in compliance with the law, The lawyer also called for institutional safeguards to protect medical practitioners who disregarded internal payment policies to fulfil their professional obligations to emergency patients. She, consequently, called for the strengthening of emergency healthcare funding, establishing effective reimbursement mechanisms as well as providing lawful avenues for recovering outstanding medical expenses. On his part, another lawyer, Mr Spurgeon Ataene, said doctors had an ethical obligation to prioritise saving lives in emergency situations before turning their attention to payment. Ataene said demanding payment before attending to a patient in a life-threatening condition, could amount to professional misconduct and potentially expose the practitioner to disciplinary action. He added that denying emergency care on financial grounds could also raise concerns about the patient’s fundamental right to life. Ataene specifically stressed that gunshot victims should be treated before questions were asked about the circumstances of their injuries. “It will therefore, be unethical for a doctor to make a demand for payment before treatment; He could be sanctioned and may lose his license,” he said Ataene, however, acknowledged that patients should pay for medical services, particularly in non-emergency situations, noting that hospitals required funds to maintain equipment, pay staff and provide a clean and orderly environment. He urged lawmakers to strengthen legislation requiring healthcare providers to stabilise emergency patients before making payment demands or conducting further inquiries that could delay treatment. Similarly, another Lagos-based lawyer, Mrs Jumoke Ajayi of Olorunwapelumi Chambers, warned that healthcare providers could face criminal sanctions for refusing emergency medical treatment over unpaid bills. Ajayi cited Section 20(2) of the National Health Act, which prescribes a fine of N100,000, imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months, or both, for contravening the provision on emergency medical treatment. She explained that patients suffering from serious injuries sustained in road accidents, severe bleeding or other life-threatening conditions were entitled to immediate medical attention, irrespective of their financial circumstances. “The legal position is that the hospital must attend to the patient’s emergency medical needs without refusing treatment on financial grounds,” she said. Ajayi, however, clarified that the law did not automatically exempt patients from paying their medical bills, adding that hospitals could subsequently seek payment for services provided, subject to applicable laws and relevant payment arrangements. According to her, determining whether a hospital or healthcare worker had committed an offence would depend on the circumstances and available evidence, including whether treatment was refused, delayed or referred to another facility. Meanwhile, Ajayi noted that healthcare workers could not be held liable for consequences arising from their inability to provide particular emergency services where a hospital lacked the necessary equipment or capacity to handle the case. Besides, she noted that the law protected patients’ access to emergency care but did not require every form of medical treatment to be provided free of charge. On the whole, the lawyers maintained that protecting patients’ lives and sustaining healthcare institutions should not be competing objectives. They consequently, urging government and relevant stakeholders to develop a system that guarantees emergency treatment while providing hospitals with adequate financial support. items.title: Three JoyNews journalists selected for exchange programme in London under UK MEET fellowship
items.description: Esther Nkrumah, Nana Boakye Yiadom and Jacqueline Ansomah Yeboah are among 10 journalists selected for the next stage of the UK MEET programme after a competitive story-pitch process. Three JoyNews journalists have been selected to travel to London for a further round of training and knowledge exchange under the UK Media and Emerging Technologies (UK MEET) programme. The programme attracted more than 500 applicants, of whom 30 were selected to participate in the fellowship. Following a series of training sessions, practical exercises and newsroom simulations, 16 participants were selected to present their proposed investigative stories before the final 10 were chosen for the UK exchange. The selected journalists will use the opportunity to deepen their understanding of science, technology and innovation reporting while developing investigations into how emerging technologies could address challenges in Ghana. Three stories, three areas of public interest Nana Boakye Yiadom’s proposed investigation will examine whether artificial intelligence can analyse satellite images to detect early signs of illegal mining in Ghana’s forest reserves. The story will explore whether Ghana is ready to invest in the technology and whether it could support a shift from reactive enforcement towards early detection and evidence-based environmental protection. Esther Nkrumah will investigate the use of drones and artificial intelligence to identify and treat mosquito breeding sites in Ada East as part of efforts to control malaria. Her reporting will examine whether the approach delivers the expected operational benefits, what residents and health workers are experiencing, and whether the intervention can ultimately contribute to reducing malaria infections. Jacqueline Ansomah Yeboah’s investigation will focus on artificial intelligence tools designed to support senior high school teachers in preparing lesson plans and assessments. The story will test whether the tools produce accurate, curriculum-aligned content and examine their usefulness, limitations and potential implications for teaching and learning in Ghana. Advancing science and technology reporting The UK MEET programme is led by Imperial Global Ghana in collaboration with Imperial College London, with support from the British High Commission. It seeks to strengthen the capacity of journalists to report on science, technology and emerging innovations with accuracy, depth and public relevance. The fellowship has included discussions with researchers, practical reporting exercises and simulations that challenged participants to verify claims, interrogate evidence and communicate complex scientific issues to the public. The London exchange will build on this experience, providing the selected journalists with a further opportunity to engage with experts and strengthen their reporting on emerging technologies. For the three JoyNews journalists, the selection marks the next step in developing investigations that examine not only the promise of innovation, but also the evidence behind it and its potential impact on communities

Beyond the headlines: How the UK MEET Fellowship is changing the way we approach Science Journalism
items.description: Five days can feel like a short time, but my experience at the UK Media and Emerging Technologies (UK MEET) Fellowship has reminded me how much can change when journalists are challenged to question what they know, interrogate evidence and approach familiar stories from a different perspective. Led by Imperial Global Ghana, with support from Imperial College London and the British High Commission, the fellowship brought together journalists and media professionals for an intensive residential programme in Accra from October 11 to 17, 2026. It explored how the media can better report on science, technology and innovation, particularly as emerging technologies increasingly shape public life. For me, it was an opportunity to look beyond the excitement surrounding discoveries and technologies and ask a more fundamental question: What does the evidence actually tell us, and what does it mean for the people affected? Learning to question the claims behind the headlines One of the most valuable aspects of the fellowship was its practical approach. Rather than relying only on presentations and discussions, we were placed in newsroom simulations that challenged us to make decisions under pressure, verify information, and distinguish confirmed facts from claims that still needed investigation. In one simulation, we had to respond to a developing heatwave story involving public health warnings, electricity supply challenges, agricultural losses, and viral misinformation. Conflicting figures from different sources forced us to consider how to report uncertainty without misleading the public. The exercise reinforced an important lesson: a compelling story is not necessarily a verified story. Journalists must establish what is known, what remains uncertain, who can independently confirm the information, and what evidence is still missing. Other exercises examined artificial intelligence and health claims, including an audit in which a vendor’s claimed AI accuracy rate differed significantly from an independently measured result. We also explored how to report on emerging technologies such as plastic-recycling innovations without simply repeating the claims of their developers. These experiences challenged us to look beyond impressive statistics and ask about methodology, independent testing, limitations, and the real-world implications of the technology. Making science relevant to everyday people The fellowship also explored climate and environmental risks, biomedical innovation, genomics, artificial intelligence and digital storytelling. A recurring lesson was the importance of translating complex research into stories audiences can understand without losing the accuracy or context that makes the information valuable. Science journalism is not simply about explaining unfamiliar terms. It involves asking the right questions, identifying whose perspectives are missing, and showing how research and innovation affect people’s everyday lives. This is particularly important in Ghana, where discussions about artificial intelligence, education, healthcare and climate change are often accompanied by big promises. Journalists have a responsibility to examine those promises, establish what the evidence supports, and help audiences understand both the opportunities and the risks. The sessions also reminded me that journalists and researchers do not have to work in separate worlds. Collaboration between the two can strengthen public understanding, provided journalists retain their independence and continue to scrutinise the evidence. Pitching a story about AI and education in Ghana Beyond the simulations, the fellowship gave participants an opportunity to develop and present story ideas that could investigate the impact of emerging technologies in their communities. My pitch focused on the use of subject-specific artificial intelligence applications by senior high school teachers in Ghana. Under the working title The Invisible Teacher?, I proposed investigating whether AI tools designed to support teachers in preparing lesson plans and assessments are accurate, aligned with Ghana’s curriculum, and genuinely useful in the classroom. The idea goes beyond the presence of technology in schools. It asks whether these tools deliver on their promises, what evidence supports their usefulness, and whether teachers and students have the resources and support needed to benefit from them. Developing and presenting the pitch challenged me to narrow the reporting question, identify the evidence required, and consider how to test the claims being made about AI in education. The process also reinforced the importance of approaching technology stories with curiosity rather than assuming that a new tool is either a solution to every problem or a threat to be rejected. From pitching to the London Knowledge Exchange One of the most exciting outcomes of the fellowship was the opportunity to compete for a place on the London Knowledge Exchange programme. After submitting our story ideas and participating in the residential programme, shortlisted participants presented their pitches to a panel. The exercise required us to communicate the central reporting question, demonstrate its public interest and explain how we intended to investigate it. I was selected as one of the final 10 participants for the London exchange programme. It is a significant milestone for me, not only because of the opportunity to travel to London, but also because the selection process pushed me to defend my ideas, think critically about my methodology and demonstrate how my proposed reporting could contribute to public understanding. It has encouraged me to keep developing stories that examine the impact of emerging technologies rather than simply report their arrival. Taking the lessons beyond the fellowship Looking back, the UK MEET Fellowship has been a reminder that journalism must continually evolve alongside the subjects it covers. As technologies become more sophisticated, journalists need the confidence to question developers, engage researchers, examine data and explain uncertainty without losing their audiences. I leave the programme with new perspectives, valuable connections and a renewed commitment to public-interest reporting. I also leave with questions I intend to carry into my newsroom: Who benefits from an innovation? What evidence demonstrates that it works? Who might be left behind? And how can we tell these stories in ways that help the public make informed decisions? The real test begins after the fellowship, when the lessons learnt must translate into stronger reporting, more rigorous verification and better storytelling. For me, the goal is clear: to tell science, technology and innovation stories that are accurate, accessible and relevant to the lives of the people they are meant to serve. Because reporting innovation should mean more than celebrating what is new. It should mean helping the public understand what works, what does not, what remains uncertain, and what it all means for their future.

items.title: Massacre du 17 octobre : de Vichy à l’OAS, Emmanuel Grégoire met en garde contre l’extrême droite
items.description: Discours émouvant et historique prononcé ce samedi par le maire de Paris Emmanuel Grégoire en hommage aux victimes des massacres du 17 octobre 1961 , avec une mise garde claire dans un contexte de montée en puissance du discours de haine et de l’extrême droite en France. La cérémonie de commémoration de ce massacre a eu lieu au Pont Saint-Michel, dans la capitale française, en présence de parlementaires, dont le sénateur écologiste Akli Mellouli, et de nombreuses personnalités, parmi lesquelles Ségolène Royal et Chems-Eddine Hafiz, le recteur de la Grande mosquée de Paris. Un jour particulier “ pour l’Algérie, pour la France et pour Paris ” Dans un long discours, le maire socialiste a évoqué un jour “si particulier pour l’Algérie, pour la France et pour Paris ”, une date où l’histoire commune entre l’Algérie et la France “ s’est écrite, comme tant d’autres fois, dans le sang ”. Il y a 65 ans, a-t-il rappelé, entre 20 000 et 30 000 hommes, femmes et enfants d’origine algérienne, ont quitté “ les bidonvilles dans lesquels on les a parqués ” pour monter à Paris dénoncer un “ couvre-feu illégal ” qui leur était imposé exclusivement. Ils étaient “ des Français Musulmans d’Algérie comme on les appelle alors, qui sont français depuis presque 100 ans, mais qui ne seront jamais des citoyens à part entière ”, a encore souligné l’élu. Deux semaines plus tôt, a-t-il encore rappelé, le préfet de police Maurice Papon déclarait aux obsèques d’un policier assassiné : “Pour un coup donné, nous en porterons dix ”. “Une rafle comme aux pires heures de notre histoire” “Ce soir-là, les forces de l’ordre n’ont pas attendu qu’un coup soit donné pour en porter dix, cent, mille, des dizaines de milliers de coups qui pleuvent sur un peuple en quête de reconnaissance et de liberté ”, a dénoncé le premier responsable de la capitale française. Le maire décrit une violence qui “ se déchaîne ”, “ les coups, les corps à terre et le sang qui commence à couler ”, “ une rafle comme aux pires heures de notre histoire ”, “ un bain de sang qui est la marque du maintien de l’ordre colonial ”. Au total, 11 578 personnes sont arrêtées. Soixante-cinq ans après, il manque toujours le nombre de morts “ 100, 200 ou plus encore ”, “ le nom de ces femmes et de ces hommes, leur identité, leur histoire ” et “ les circonstances exactes de leur mort ”. Ce qui manque aussi aujourd’hui, “ c’est une voix, celle de la France ”, a dit Emmanuel Grégoire, estimant qu’il ne s’agit pas d’un oubli, mais d'un “ effacement, une dissimulation, un mensonge d’État pour cacher un crime d’État ”. Cette même violence revient aujourd’hui “ attisée par le discours de haine ” Réitérant l’appel qu'il a lancé cette semaine avec une trentaine de maires pour “ la reconnaissance pleine et entière du massacre du 17 octobre 1961 comme un crime d'État ”, Grégoire a indiqué qu’il faut “ regarder notre histoire en face, même quand elle nous fait honte ”, car, a-t-il poursuivi, “ prolonger le silence qui a suivi le massacre des Algériens, c’est faire de nous les complices de ce crime quand nous n’en sommes que les héritiers ”. Le maire a invoqué l'histoire avec un clin d'œil à l’actualité en rappelant que “ce massacre n’est pas seulement lié à la guerre d’indépendance algérienne ”, mais “ remonte bien plus loin dans la culture française de l’autorité et de l’ordre, dans l’histoire de l’extrême droite ”. C'est cette même violence qui “ revient aujourd’hui décomplexée, débridée, attisée par les discours de haine qui ne retiennent plus leurs mots ”. Or, a mis en garde le maire de Paris, “ quand on ne retient plus ses mots aujourd’hui, on ne retiendra pas ses coups demain ”. Alors que l’extrême droite est plus que jamais aux portes de l’Élysée, Emmanuel Grégoire a adressé un message à celles et ceux qui disent : « on n’a jamais essayé », en leur affirmant : « il faut leur rappeler l’affaire Dreyfus, il faut leur rappeler la ligue d’action française, il faut leur rappeler la collaboration, il faut leur rappeler Vichy, il faut leur rappeler l’OAS, il faut leur rappeler le 17 octobre 1961 ». Pour Emmanuel Grégoire, le 17 octobre 1961, « doit entrer dans la mémoire de France comme elle a trouvé sa place dans la pierre de Paris ». « Le sang des Algériens qui a rougi la Seine ce soir-là, doit maintenant noircir les pages de nos livres d’histoire », a-t-il soutenu, en appelant à faire de ce 17 octobre un « jour de commémoration nationale ». Présente sur les lieux, Ségolène Royal a salué le « message fort et émouvant » du maire de Paris Emmanuel Grégoire, pour les « nombreuses victimes algériennes et françaises de la sanglante répression, crime d’État du préfet Papon contre une manifestation « . L’article Massacre du 17 octobre : de Vichy à l'OAS, Emmanuel Grégoire met en garde contre l'extrême droite est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Egypt’s president says country ready to defend Saudi Arabia ‘if requested’
items.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Saturday said Egypt was ready to defend Saudi Arabia “if requested”, as fighting flares between the kingdom and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. Since Yemen’s war reignited in July, the Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week. The Houthis have also blockaded the Bab al-Mandab Strait, piling pressure on energy exports as Iran presses its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian military academy, Sisi said Egypt was “not looking for a role to play” in regional conflicts, but added that it was “inconceivable” for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was “harmed or its security and stability threatened”. “Egypt, of course, with the directives of His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will carry out any measure to protect you or defend you,” he said. He added that any deployment would require parliamentary approval and said he hoped lawmakers would convene in an emergency session to grant authorisation “if it is requested of us”. “I’m not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone,” Sisi said. “We are speaking only about defence.” During a visit to Egypt last month, de facto Saudi leader Mohammed bin Salman and Sisi called for free and secure navigation in the Red Sea, a vital trade route. The conflict with the Houthis poses risks not only to Saudi Arabia’s security and energy exports, but also to Egypt, where disruption to Red Sea shipping could further reduce revenues from the Suez Canal, a key source of foreign currency. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said last month that Egypt’s Suez Canal lost about $11 billion in revenues since the Houthis began attacking commercial vessels following Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack on Israel. Despite its longstanding military ties with Gulf states, Egypt has not joined the Mecca agreement, a mutual defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan in August, with Cairo generally favouring diplomacy over participation in regional military alliances. Saudi Arabia has long been a key backer of Egypt, providing financial support after the 2013 ouster of Islamist late president Mohammed Morsi and during subsequent economic crises. The post Egypt’s president says country ready to defend Saudi Arabia ‘if requested’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La rabia de los estudiantes y la violencia policial incendian Francia
items.description: La rabia ha vuelto este sábado a las calles de Francia. Estudiantes, funcionarios, transportistas y el espectro de los chalecos amarillos acudieron masivamente a la cita en unos 500 puntos del país . La movilización social, convocada originalmente contra el encarecimiento del coste de la vida y la pérdida de poder adquisitivo, a la que después se sumaron los estudiantes, ha terminado incendiando las calles de las grandes ciudades de Francia. El presidente de la República, Emmanuel Macron , llamó a la calma el viernes por la noche. No sirvió de nada, como la mayoría de su acción de gobierno en el último año. La policía cargó violentamente contra los manifestantes con pelotas de goma, gases lacrimógenos y cañones de agua en las principales ciudades del país, cuyas calles empezaron a arder pasadas las dos de la tarde.
