items.title: Coopération Togo-Russie : Une exposition photographique à Lomé en prélude au 3ᵉ Sommet de Moscou
items.description: Lomé, 17 oct. (ATOP) – Une exposition photographique, retraçant la dynamique des relations entre la Fédération de Russie, le Togo et l’ensemble du continent africain, a été organisée le vendredi 16 octobre à la Maison de la Russie à Lomé. Placé sous le thème « Regard croisé à venir partager », cet événement culturel et diplomatique préfigure le troisième Sommet Russie-Afrique prévu les 28 et 29 octobre prochains à Moscou. Il est porté conjointement par l’Ambassade de la Fédération de Russie au Togo, l’Association Alternative Russo-Togolaise, « African Initiative » et l’agence de presse TASS. La cérémonie a rassemblé plusieurs personnalités diplomatiques, administratives et communautaires, dont l’ambassadeur de Russie au Togo, Igor Nikolaïevitch Evdokimov, ainsi que des représentants d’organisations de la société civile. Discours de l’Ambassadeur La visite guidée de l’exposition a permis au public de découvrir 24 clichés illustrant les moments forts du partenariat russo-africain. Les photos immortalisent notamment des rencontres au sommet entre le Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, et son homologue russe, Vladimir Poutine, ainsi que les entretiens diplomatiques menés par le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Robert Dussey, avec son homologue russe, Sergueï Lavrov. Au-delà de la politique institutionnelle, l’exposition a mis en relief la coopération scientifique, technologique et industrielle. Les présentations ont porté également sur le renforcement des capacités académiques avec l’attribution de 180 bourses d’études aux étudiants togolais, orientés prioritairement vers les filières scientifiques, technologiques, médicales et l’innovation robotique. Un partenariat politique et institutionnel en pleine expansion L’ambassadeur Evdokimov a rappelé que cette exposition intervient après la tenue à Lomé, du 29 septembre au 1ᵉʳ octobre 2026, de la première session de la commission mixte intergouvernementale chargée du suivi de l’accord de coopération bilatérale. « Cette rencontre de haut niveau a permis d’examiner plusieurs dossiers d’intérêt commun en vue de donner un contenu concret à la coopération entre le Togo et la Russie », a souligné le diplomate russe, précisant que la prochaine échéance moscovite permettra d’approfondir ce dialogue stratégique. Le président de l’Association Alternative Russo-Togolaise, Pascal Bidjakine, a présenté les activités de la Maison de la Russie, ouverte le 26 juin dernier. Il a indiqué que l’institution propose des cours de langue russe et des initiations au jeu d’échecs. M. Bidjakine a rappelé que la Russie, à l’instar du Togo, est une mosaïque de peuples et de régions vivant en harmonie, promouvant ainsi des échanges interpersonnels constructifs. Le représentant de l’agence de presse TASS, M. Andrei Belonogov, a rappelé la portée historique de ces archives visuelles capturées par la plus ancienne agence de presse russe lors des sommets de Sotchi (2019) et de Saint-Pétersbourg (2023). Le premier adjoint au maire de la commune Golfe 2, Dr Assiah Sylvestre a salué les associations et partenaires russes pour leurs actions en faveur du développement de la commune en particulier et du Togo en général. Il cité quelques actions, entre autres, la distribution de cadeaux et le soutien à plus d’une trentaine d’enfants vulnérables, l’organisation de concours d’émulation en mathématiques pour les jeunes talents, la participation active aux opérations communautaires de salubrité publique dans les quartiers de la commune. « Nous souhaitons vivement que cette coopération continue d’apporter sa pierre au développement de notre pays », a déclaré Dr Assiah. Le troisième Sommet Russie-Afrique, qui se tiendra à Moscou les 28 et 29 octobre prochain, marquera une étape supplémentaire dans la consolidation de ces partenariats multisectoriels et de la gouvernance partagée entre la Fédération de Russie et le Togo. ATOP/SED/BA

items.title: L’avantage des rues en pavé (Par Maguette NDONG)
items.description: C’est un secret de Polichinelle, nos routes et nos ruelles sont en mauvais état au Sénégal. Il suffit de faire un tour dans nos quartiers pour faire le constat. Il y a partout des nids de poule ou parfois des trous béants qui datent de Mathusalem. Des années durant, piétons et automobiles empruntent ces chemins en subissant les mêmes désagréments, à savoir panne, inconfort et parfois même des accidents peuvent se produire. Il arrive toutefois que certains jeunes fouettés par leur orgueil prennent des pelles et des coups de marteau pour essayer de colmater ces brèches. Quoique salutaires, ces actions citoyennes ne peuvent jamais changer les choses. Finalement, tout le monde semble se résigner à cette situation pitoyable. Quand l’hivernage arrive, certains quartiers sont invivables. Ça dégouline, ça pue. Là où il y avait un trou s’installe une mare fétide et nauséabonde. Les conducteurs qui craignent pour leur engin sont obligés de faire des détours ou de créer des voies nouvelles à l’intérieur des quartiers pour pouvoir passer. Bref, c’est toujours la grande galère. Seulement, depuis quelque temps, certaines collectivités territoriales du pays construisent des routes en pavés dans le but de panser ces plaies béantes qui défigurent nos quartiers. Le pavage est devenu une nouvelle trouvaille pour colmater les brèches et soulager les populations. Ces nouvelles routes baptisées « Tally carreaux » changent radicalement la physionomie de nos quartiers et de nos villes. Car, elles favorisent l’installation de nouveaux commerces à savoir boutiques, restaurants et boulangeries etc. Avec ces nouvelles rues, la mobilité des citoyens devient facile et fluide. C’est dire que la route est un ferment pour développer l’économie locale.Aujourd’hui, dans la plupart des budgets votés dans nos communes, le pavage de quelques routes figure en bonne place. Lors de son passage à la Ville de Dakar, l’ancien maire Khalifa Sall avait initié un important programme de pavage des routes stratégiques. Ledit programme avait changé radicalement le visage de la capitale sénégalaise. Depuis lors, l’idée a fait tache d’huile dans d’autres communes sénégalaises. Récemment, lors de son passage à Genève, au 6e Forum des maires des Nations Unies, Alioune Pouye, le maire de Sébikotane a démontré l’importance du pavage pour sa Municipalité. « Nous avons obtenu des résultats importants parce que le fait d’avoir revêtu les rues en pavés a facilité le déplacement des personnes à mobilité réduite qui, auparavant, ne pouvaient pas se déplacer sur le sable. Aujourd’hui, elles peuvent se déplacer avec leurs chaises roulantes sur les rues en pavés », a dit l’édile de Sébikotane. D’ailleurs, sur les dix-huit quartiers que compte cette commune, les huit sont maintenant en pavé. Également, des programmes de l’État tels que le Promovilles ont intégré le pavage dans la liste des réalisations à faire pour les communes bénéficiaires. C’est dire que nos élus sont résolument engagés à remplacer les trous béants et les mares par les pavés. En jetant les pavés dans la mare, nos élus entendent mettre fin aux désagréments causés par le mauvais état de nos routes et offrir de meilleures conditions de vie aux populations. maguette.ndong@lesoleil.sn

Sédhiou: « Nous sommes la solution » plaide pour une alimentation saine et locale
items.description: Plusieurs femmes ont pris part à cette journée dans la région de Sédhiou. Une célébration marquée par des causeries et des sensibilisations sur les enjeux d’une alimentation saine. Sédhiou-A l’extérieur du jardin de la place de l’indépendances de Sédhiou, des femmes de différentes communautés rivalisent, servant de la gastronomie locale. Des plats africains d’origines gambienne, Bissau guinéenne, sénégalaise, ivoirienne, un régal pour marquer la journée mondiale de l’alimentation, célébrée dans le Pakao par le mouvement panafricain « nous sommes la solution », qui est aussi s'engager, depuis sa création, à la promotion de la bonne pratique basée sur la souveraineté alimentaire en Afrique. Visiblement satisfaite de la mobilisation, Mariama Sonko, président de ce mouvement panafricain, a souligné que cette journée dédiée à la célébration de l’alimentation est importante, car c’est la femme qui est actrice de l’alimentation, elle est de la production à la consommation. Poursuivant son propos elle ajoute : « L’alimentation est basée entre les mains de la femme autrement dit, le savoir et le savoir-faire sont entre ses mains ». Cependant, de nos jours, il y a une prolifération de maladies qui ne dit pas son nom. Des symptômes méconnus de nos ancêtres. « Cela est dû à une mauvaise alimentation », a affirmé M. Sonko, invitant dans le même sillage à la conscientisation de la femme sur les enjeux de l’alimentation. Toujours dans une volonté de promouvoir les pratiques endogènes de l’alimentation, Nous sommes la solution et ses différentes associations sont allées plus loin, en se penchant sur la transformation des aliments, « nous sommes la solution a mis en place un bouillon à base de produit locaux appelé « soumpac », ce produit bio, explique Mariama Sonko, est la conclusion des études sur ce qu’utilisaient les ancêtres pour donner du goût à leur repas avant l’arrivée des bouillons en Afrique dans les années 1970. La leader de Nous sommes la solution a profité de cette tribune plaidant pour l’accès des femmes rurales au foncier. Jonas Souloubany BASSENE (correspondant)

items.title: CAN at 50: Church must challenge govt, defend Nigerians — Archbishop Okoh
items.description: …As First Lady urges Christians to sustain unity …Honours Gowon, OBJ, Osinbajo, others By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja President of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Archbishop Daniel Okoh, has charged the Church to challenge government failures, defend vulnerable Nigerians and resist political capture, declaring that it must not surrender its prophetic responsibility for the sake of political convenience. Speaking at CAN’s 50th anniversary celebration in Abuja on Saturday, Archbishop Okoh said the Church must adopt a more courageous, evidence-based and constructive approach to national affairs, holding those in power accountable while supporting policies that advance the common good. In his homily, themed “CAN at 50: A Prophetic Voice of Hope,” the CAN president said the Church must remain independent, morally alert and committed to speaking for Nigerians whose voices are often ignored. “The Church must speak!” he declared. Archbishop Okoh listed internally displaced persons, children denied education, unemployed youths, farmers unable to access their farmlands because of insecurity, women facing violence and victims of human trafficking among those whose plight the Church must address. He warned, however, that speaking prophetically did not mean opposing every government policy or turning the Church into a partisan platform. “A responsible watchman must be accurate. He should not raise alarm simply because he dislikes a policy or disagrees with a political leader,” he said. On the relationship between the Church and government, Archbishop Okoh advocated what he called critical collaboration, urging Christian leaders to commend good policies and challenge failures without compromising their independence. “Collaborate where common good requires it, challenge where justice requires challenge, commend where government does well and warn where government fails, while maintaining the Church’s independence,” he said. He said the next 50 years of CAN should be marked by stronger research, advocacy, institutional maturity and collective action, with greater attention to justice, human dignity, democratic institutions, religious freedom and the welfare of vulnerable citizens. Archbishop Okoh also urged Christians to preserve the unity that inspired CAN’s founding in August 1976, warning that denominational rivalries could weaken the Church’s collective voice. He recalled that the Association’s early years were marked by mutual suspicion and the marginalisation of some Christian traditions, but said successive leaders had worked to build a more inclusive platform. “At 50, all the church traditions in Nigeria are represented in CAN through the following major blocs: CSN, CCN, CPFN/PFN, OAIC and TEKAN/ECWA. The last time I checked, no one is missing on the table,” he said. The CAN president cautioned Christians against taking that unity for granted or allowing disagreements, particularly on social media, to undermine their fellowship. He stressed that CAN belonged to every believer, not just its elected and appointed officers, and urged members to break down remaining barriers between denominations. Drawing on the biblical image of a watchman, Archbishop Okoh said the Church had a duty to identify threats to justice and human dignity, warn those in authority and defend citizens whose circumstances left them vulnerable. He also called on Christians to match their prayers for Nigeria with practical action, integrity and responsible leadership. “Nigeria can be better — Nigeria will be better! But hope requires responsibility: prayer must be accompanied by positive action, faith by integrity, leadership by accountability and freedom by responsibility,” he said. Archbishop Okoh said the jubilee must serve as the beginning of a renewed national mission, with the Church expected to defend human dignity, demand accountability and contribute to national development. Christians Must Sustain Unity – Mrs Tinubu The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, congratulated CAN on its 50 years of service to God and humanity, urging Christian denominations to sustain their unity. She said the anniversary theme, “Walking Together in Faith,” reflected Christ’s prayer for the unity of believers. “I pray that, just as Christ prayed for the saints, all the Christian blocs and denominations will continue to remain united in Jesus’ name,” she said. The golden jubilee celebration also featured awards recognising prominent Nigerians and public office holders for their contributions to the Church and society. Honours as List Former Head of State, General Yakubu Gowon; former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo and Goodluck Jonathan; and former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo were listed among recipients of the Pillar of Faith awards. Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives Benjamin Kalu, Secretary to the Government of the Federation George Akume, several state governors and other public officials were listed in the Christian Icon category. The programme also featured prayers for Nigeria and its leaders, the presentation of CAN’s history book and the launch of a proposed airport chapel project. The post CAN at 50: Church must challenge govt, defend Nigerians — Archbishop Okoh appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Imran being forced into Benazir, Nawaz-style deal, claims Achakzai
items.description: • Demands authorities disclose whereabouts of Sohail Afridi • Mengal says those claiming to be framers of Constitution are ‘trampling it’ • TTAP alliance challenges governor’s rule, emergency before Peshawar High Court PESHAWAR: PTI fou­nder Imran Khan is being forced into an agreement, similar to those given to former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto, Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai claimed on Friday. The opposition leader was referring to the arrangements whereby the two former PMs went into self-imposed exile following their respective ousters. Mr Sharif, who was ousted and imprisoned following a military coup by then-army chief Pervez Musharraf, left the country in 2000 following a deal negotiated by Saudi and Lebanese leaders. Benazir, meanwhile, voluntarily went into self-exile after her party lost the 1997 general elections following her dismissal by then-president Farooq Leg­hari. At the time, her husband Asif Zardari was imprisoned over corruption charges, and was finally released in 2004. “The same is happening today with the PML-N and PPP in government,” Mr Achakzai said at a news conference at the Peshawar High Court (PHC). He was accompanied by Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) leaders Sardar Akhtar Mengal and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas. He said they were in contact with all opposition parties and would soon convene a multi-party conference. Resigning from the assemblies was also an option, he said, adding that they had submitted their demands in response to the offer of negotiations. “Nowhere in the world is a prisoner denied meetings,” he said, calling for the withdrawal of the “wrong amen­dment”, empow­erment of parliament and the formation of an independent commission to ensure transparent elections. He said no problem could be resolved until parliament was empowered. Expressing concern over the whereabouts of the KP chief minister and other lawmakers, he demanded that the authorities disclose the chief minister’s whereabouts, calling it their constitutional right to know. “We stand with the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The people of this province have the first right over its minerals. Regardless of political affiliation, everyone must unite for the homeland,” he said, adding that they would be safer if the country survived. Mr Mengal said those claiming to be the framers of the Constitution were trampling on it. He questioned the imposition of governor’s rule in KP on the grounds of terrorism, asking whether military operations had improved or worsened conditions in Balochistan. He said KP’s elected chief minister had been removed, while the provincial assembly speaker and a minister were missing. Those who had won the general elections on Form 47 had become members of the National Assembly, he alleged, adding that the system could not continue this way. Raja Nasir Abbas, the opposition leader in the Senate, said lawlessness had reached its peak. “You cannot run a country, yet you have occupied a province,” he told reporters, adding that a cabinet member had himself acknowledged that the system had collapsed. TTAP challenges governor’s rule Meanwhile on Friday, TTAP leaders challenged the proclamation of emergency and imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa before the PHC, seeking to have the measures declared unconstitutional and illegal. The constitutional petition was jointly filed by TTAP Chairman Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Vice Chairman Senator Raja Nasir Abbas, Balochistan National Party-Mengal chief Sardar Akhtar Mengal and Sindh United Party President Syed Zainul Abideen through Advocates Muazzam Butt and Baseem Ahmad Siddiqui. The court was requested to declare the Oct 11 proclamation of emergency, issued under Articles 232(1) and 234 of the Constitution, unconstitutional and without lawful authority, arguing that the required constitutional conditions had not been met or that the measures exceeded the powers conferred by the Constitution. They challenged the purported transfer of the KP Assembly’s legislative powers to parliament and the displacement of the elected chief minister and provincial cabinet. They also sought the annulment of executive orders and notifications that depended on the validity of the proclamation. The petitioners also challenged the establishment of the purported KP Advisory Council and Area Development Secretariat, arguing that these bodies could not exercise powers beyond those conferred by the Constitution or replace established provincial institutions. They questioned any purported suspension of constitutional provisions, including Article 175(3), unless expressly authorised by the Constitution. The petitioners sought annulment of the Oct 11 notification concerning the deployment of armed forces in the province to the extent where it violated Article 245, failed to meet constitutional requirements or exceeded the scope of the provision. They also sought directions to ensure that elected representatives and constitutionally established institutions in KP were not unlawfully prevented from performing their functions and that no elected representative was detained or restrained except in accordance with the Constitution. Pending a final decision, they sought interim relief to suspend or restrain the impugned measures to prevent the displacement of elected institutions, transfer of legislative authority, creation of parallel executive structures or other irreparable harm, subject to the court’s assessment of constitutional requirements and public safety. Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

items.title: Islamabad ATC rejects police request for physical remand of ex-GB CM Khalid Khurshid
items.description: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday rejected the police’s request for 30-day physical remand of PTI leader and former Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister Khalid Khurshid and sent him to jail on judicial remand in connection with a case registered over the November 26 protest. Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain heard the case against Khurshid. During the hearing, Islamabad police produced the PTI leader before the court and sought his physical remand for 30 days. However, the court turned down the request and directed that he be sent to judicial custody. A case was registered against Khurshid, the president of the PTI’s GB chapter, at Aabpara Police Station in connection with the party’s November 26 protest in 2024. The protest saw more than 10,000 PTI protesters surge into Islamabad, defying a ban on public gatherings and a lockdown to skirmish with 20,000 security forces enlisted to turn them back. A day of clashes between security forces and protesters in the city’s Red Zone had ended in the PTI leadership’s hasty retreat, with the party announcing that it was calling off its planned protest sit-in “for the time being”. Subsequently, cases were registered against several PTI leaders under various sections of the Pakistan Penal Code and Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act. Khurshid was arrested along with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and several others at the speaker’s house in Peshawar, according to the PTI, shortly after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11. Sources said Khurshid had been staying at the KP chief minister’s residence since 2023 to avoid arrest by GB police. PTI workers discharged In a separate development, the court also discharged PTI workers arrested in connection with two cases linked to the party’s recent long march after rejecting a request by the investigating officer for an adjournment to conduct their identification parade. During proceedings concerning the PTI workers arrested in two cases registered at Shalimar and Secretariat police stations, the investigating officer requested an adjournment to conduct an identification parade. However, the defence counsel opposed the request, arguing that the workers had already spent more than 40 days in custody and that the police had repeatedly sought adjournments without producing them before the court. The lawyers maintained that the accused were innocent and had been deliberately implicated in the cases, alleging that the police arbitrarily arrested individuals and falsely portrayed them as PTI workers. The defence counsel reiterated their earlier plea for the discharge of the accused and urged the court to implement its order passed at the previous hearing. Accepting the defence’s arguments, the court ordered the discharge of all the PTI workers from the cases. The workers had been placed in judicial custody for the purpose of an identification parade in connection with the cases registered at Shalimar and Secretariat police stations.

items.title: Neto double gives Chelsea win; marred by Martinez injury
items.description: Pedro Neto’s double condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as Chelsea won 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite the loss of goalkeeper Emi Martinez to a head injury. Neto opened the scoring inside the first minute of the second half and secured the three points during the 11 added minutes following the lengthy treatment given to the stricken Martinez. The Argentine international was involved in a sickening head clash with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital. Victory lifts Chelsea above the Toffees into the top four of the Premier League. After a slow start, a fiery-tempered encounter sparked into life when Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong launched into a tackle on Josh Acheampong for the first of five first-half yellow cards. That challenge also enlivened the home crowd and spurred Everton on to their best spell of the game. Thierno Barry was guilty of another wasteful day in front of goal as the Frenchman planted a header from Jack Grealish’s cross too close to Martinez. Chelsea have made a habit of fast starts under Xabi Alonso, but it took until four minutes before half-time to threaten when Moises Caicedo blasted off the bar from a well-worked corner. Everton were furious that Morgan Rogers escaped a second booking just before the break after a thunderous clash with England team-mate James Garner. That proved to be a huge decision as the visitors this time flew out of the blocks at the start of the second period. Jorrel Hato got to the byline and his low cross fell to Neto, who had time to control before firing low past Pickford. Chelsea had not kept a Premier League clean sheet in 22 matches stretching back to January, but were rarely troubled by an Everton side short on forward options despite the loss of Martinez. The treatment for the goalkeeper threatened to halt Chelsea’s momentum as they controlled the second half. Belgian Mike Penders replaced Martinez for his first Premier League appearance but had little to do bar dealing with a few desperate Everton crosses. At the other end Pickford made a fine save to deny Joao Pedro. But Chelsea did get their second goal when Neto coolly stroked into the bottom corner after Jordan Henderson’s free-kick was blocked by the Everton wall. items.title: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict
items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran supports a “political process” to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi rebels. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a major attack last week. “We support an inclusive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue,” Araghchi said in a speech at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad. Araghchi repeated Iran’s offer to mediate between the two sides. Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh previously said Riyadh has not responded to Iran’s overture. On Friday, Iran denied having anything to do with the Houthi attacks, after Saudi Arabia accused Tehran of encouraging the group’s escalation. In his speech, Araghchi also said “either we build security together, or we will endure insecurity together,” adding that Tehran was willing “to cooperate with all its brothers and neighbours to achieve the first option”. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July. On Wednesday, Yemen’s Houthi rebels said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in Riyadh housing the energy giant’s operations centre. Powerful explosions also rattled the Saudi capital, as the coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a missile fired by the group towards Riyadh. On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen, targeting fuel and energy facilities it said were being used to support missile and drone attacks, as the Yemeni group threatened a “harsh and painful” response against Saudi airports, refineries and oil installations. Hours later, Saudi authorities issued warnings of potential hostile aerial threats in the kingdom’s eastern province and Riyadh. Loud explosions were heard near Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran, according to witnesses. Later, a Saudi energy ministry official confirmed the attack. Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency said that four people — two women, a man and a child — were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles in the capital and that 15 homes were damaged.

items.title: Faranah : lancement du concours de recrutement des enseignants, plus de 3 300 candidats en lice
items.description: Les épreuves du concours de recrutement de 6 000 nouveaux enseignants à la Fonction publique ont été lancées ce samedi 17 octobre 2026 à Faranah. Au total, 3 343 candidats sont répartis dans huit centres d’examen de la région. Les autorités locales saluent les dispositions prises pour assurer le bon déroulement des épreuves. Le centre Karamoko Kourouma a servi de cadre au lancement officiel des épreuves du concours de recrutement des enseignants à Faranah. Des autorités administratives et éducatives, ainsi que des candidats venus des différentes préfectures de la région, ont pris part à cette cérémonie. Sur le terrain, Pierre Touré, chef de mission des superviseurs du concours, s’est réjoui des dispositions mises en place pour garantir le bon déroulement des épreuves. « Le constat est que toutes les dispositions ont été prises pour la réussite de ce concours. Faranah compte 3 343 candidats répartis dans huit centres », a-t-il indiqué. Il a également souligné la présence des autorités régionales et éducatives, précisant que les centres étaient bien identifiés, les salles aménagées et les candidats prêts à composer. De son côté, le gouverneur de la région administrative de Faranah, le contrôleur général de police Lamine Keïta, a exprimé sa satisfaction face à la mobilisation observée. « C’est pour moi un sentiment de satisfaction de constater qu’il y a une forte mobilisation, un fort engouement au niveau de tous les candidats qui ont postulé et qui sont présents ce matin massivement dans les salles de classe », a-t-il déclaré. Le gouverneur a également assuré que les dispositifs sécuritaires prévus étaient respectés. Il a invité les candidats à faire preuve de concentration, de discipline et à respecter les règles établies pour le concours. Évoquant les objectifs de ce recrutement, Lamine Keïta a rappelé la volonté du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, de renforcer le système éducatif guinéen. « Une nation se ressentir par son système éducatif, par la formation de la jeunesse », a-t-il affirmé, avant de souligner l’importance de l’intégration de 6 000 nouveaux enseignants pour contribuer à l’amélioration de l’éducation dans le pays. Du côté des candidats, l’optimisme est également au rendez-vous. Mamadou Lao Diallo, l’un des postulants, s’est dit prêt à affronter les épreuves dans de bonnes conditions. « L’engouement est là et nous sommes venus pour pouvoir passer le concours dans de meilleures conditions. Nous sommes prêts à affronter les épreuves. Nous souhaitons bonne chance à tous les candidats », a-t-il confié. Les épreuves se déroulent ainsi dans la région de Faranah dans un contexte marqué par une forte mobilisation des candidats et la volonté des autorités de garantir la transparence du processus de recrutement. items.title: FG destroys over 19,000 illicit weapons in anti-terrorism drive — Ribadu
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki The Federal Government has disclosed that it has destroyed more than 19,000 illicit weapons since 2022 as part of sustained efforts to dismantle the operational capacity of terrorists, bandits and other criminal networks threatening Nigeria’s security. The National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, disclosed this on Saturday in Sokoto during a high-level brainstorming session on tackling banditry in Sokoto State, stressing that the government was intensifying efforts to stem the proliferation of illegal firearms and restore lasting peace to vulnerable communities. The dialogue, themed “Coping with Banditry in Sokoto State: A Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue for Prevention, Containment and Community Resilience,” was convened by the Sokoto Advancement Forum (SAF) in collaboration with the Centre for Peace Studies, Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto. It brought security concerns, community resilience and coordinated action to the forefront of discussions on addressing insecurity in the North-West. Ribadu, who was represented by Barrister Zakariyya Mijinyawa, said the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was strengthening the national security architecture through intensified military operations, intelligence gathering, law enforcement, border surveillance and improved inter-agency collaboration. He maintained that defeating banditry required a coordinated strategy capable of dismantling criminal networks, disrupting their supply chains and preventing armed groups from exploiting security gaps. He identified Operation FANSAN YAMMA as a critical platform for coordinating security operations across the North-West, noting that sustained pressure on criminal elements remained necessary to protect lives, secure communities and prevent armed groups from establishing safe havens. He said the government would continue to reinforce operational cooperation among security agencies to confront emerging threats across the region. Highlighting recent weapons-control operations, the NSA cited figures from the National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons (NCCSALW), whose Director-General, retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police Johnson Kokumo, was identified in his remarks. According to Ribadu, the centre recovered 5,449 firearms and destroyed 1,419 illicit weapons during nationwide operations in September 2026, underscoring the continuing challenge posed by illegal arms trafficking. “These figures demonstrate the importance of sustained weapons-control operations. The NCCSALW and relevant security agencies will continue to strengthen efforts to disrupt arms-trafficking networks, trace recovered weapons and prevent illicit firearms from reaching criminal groups,” he said. Ribadu, however, cautioned that military action and weapons seizures alone would not deliver sustainable peace unless accompanied by effective governance and a sustained government presence in communities recovered from criminal groups. He argued that security operations must be backed by measures that restore public confidence, rebuild local institutions and enable displaced and vulnerable populations to resume their normal lives without the constant threat of violence. To strengthen coordination, he said the Office of the National Security Adviser was advancing a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach through the National Crisis Management Doctrine (NCMD). The framework, he explained, was designed to improve preparedness, strengthen collaboration among relevant institutions and ensure that security responses were coordinated rather than fragmented across government agencies and community structures. Addressing the peculiar security challenges confronting Sokoto State, Ribadu called for intelligence-led operations to deny bandits access to safe havens around vulnerable settlements, forest corridors and border communities. He stressed the importance of supporting State Forest Guards and NSCDC Agro-Rangers as part of broader efforts to improve surveillance, protect rural populations and disrupt the movement of criminal groups. He also underscored the need for stronger cross-border intelligence-sharing and functional early-warning mechanisms linking local authorities, traditional rulers, community leaders and security focal points. According to him, timely reporting and rapid responses to credible security alerts would be crucial to preventing attacks and protecting residents in vulnerable areas, including Sabon Birni, Isa, Tangaza and Goronyo. The NSA further called for stronger community participation in the fight against banditry, warning that misinformation, economic hardship and the vulnerability of young people could undermine security interventions if left unaddressed. He urged stakeholders to protect livelihoods, expand access to education and employment opportunities, and develop community-based measures capable of discouraging youth recruitment into criminal networks. “Reintegration must never replace justice or reward violence. National security frameworks can succeed only when communities help translate them into local action,” Ribadu declared, emphasising that reconciliation and rehabilitation efforts must operate within the framework of accountability and the rule of law. His position highlighted the need to balance opportunities for peace with justice for victims and measures to prevent the recurrence of violence. He commended the Sokoto Advancement Forum (SAF) for developing its Blueprint for the Strategic Development of Sokoto State, urging participants to translate the dialogue into measurable actions rather than allowing the discussions to end as another policy exercise without practical consequences. He specifically called for the development of a community security and early-warning plan that would establish clear responsibilities, improve information-sharing and strengthen cooperation between residents and security agencies. “Let this dialogue mark a decisive step towards a safer Sokoto where communities live without fear, agriculture and commerce flourish, young people pursue productive lives, and public institutions protect every citizen,” Ribadu said. He maintained that restoring security in Sokoto and the wider North-West would require sustained commitment, collective responsibility and a comprehensive strategy that combines military pressure, intelligence-driven policing, effective governance, economic opportunity and community resilience. The post FG destroys over 19,000 illicit weapons in anti-terrorism drive — Ribadu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maroc : Amnesty International dénonce un système de surveillance visant les défenseurs des droits humains
items.description: Amnesty International denonce l'existence d'un vaste systeme de surveillance au Maroc, destine, selon l'organisation, a harceler, discrediter et reduire au silence les defenseurs des droits humains et les journalistes critiques du pouvoir. Dans un rapport intitule « On commence par le verdict », l'ONG decrit les methodes attribuees a la Direction generale de la surveillance du territoire (DGST), les services de renseignement interieur marocains, et le role d'entreprises privees dans la fourniture des technologies utilisees. Le document s'appuie notamment sur des temoignages d'anciens membres des services de renseignement, des documents internes divulgues et des enquetes journalistiques. Selon Amnesty International, les operations decrites associent des logiciels espions comme Pegasus, des interceptions de communications, le suivi des deplacements, des enregistrements clandestins et le recours a des informateurs. L'organisation affirme que ces pratiques ne se limitent pas a la collecte de donnees, mais servent egalement a alimenter des campagnes de denigrement dans des medias proches du pouvoir et sur les reseaux sociaux. Des informations privees, parfois intimes, seraient utilisees pour porter atteinte a la reputation des personnes ciblees et dissuader d'autres voix critiques de s'exprimer. Pegasus et plusieurs entreprises de surveillance cites Le rapport revient notamment sur le cas de Maâti Monjib, historien et defenseur des droits humains, presente comme l'une des premieres cibles de Pegasus au Maroc en 2017. Amnesty affirme que les autorites marocaines ont utilise ce logiciel espion entre 2017 et 2021, voire au-dela, malgre leurs dementis. L'ONG cite egalement plusieurs entreprises fournissant des technologies de surveillance, notamment la firme israelienne NSO Group, qui developpe Pegasus, l'italienne Hacking Team, l'entreprise francaise Amesys et une societe israelienne, Cellebrite. Le rapport evoque aussi des outils permettant l'interception de communications a grande echelle et le suivi des telephones mobiles. Amnesty estime qu'est ainsi instauree une combinaison faite de surveillance, harcelement judiciaire et campagnes de denigrement portant atteinte a la vie privee, a la liberte d'expression et a la liberte d'association. L'organisation souligne egalement les consequences de cses pratiques sur les familles et les reseaux professionnels des personnes visees. Appels a des enquetes independantes L'ONG demande aux autorites marocaines de mettre fin a la surveillance des journalistes et des defenseurs des droits humains, de mener des enquetes independantes sur les abus presumes et de garantir des recours aux victimes. Elle appelle egalement a reformer le cadre juridique encadrant la surveillance et recommande aux etats ainsi qu'aux entreprises concernees de suspendre certaines ventes et transferts de technologies tant que des garanties suffisantes contre les violations des droits humains ne sont pas etablies. Selon ce rapport, Amnesty International avait transmis ses conclusions aux autorites marocaines avant sa publication et les avait invitees a repondre. L'organisation indique n'avoir recu aucune reponse.

items.title: Ex-Senegal president Macky Sall withdraws as candidate for UN leader
items.description: Former president of Senegal Macky Sall on Saturday withdrew from the seven-person race to be the next UN secretary-general, a day after an informal UN Security Council poll produced no clear favourite. In a statement released on social media, Sall said he had noted the result of the poll and “hoped to contribute now the emergence of a consensus candidate within the Security Council”. He added that “the results of different test votes indicate a choice favouring a candidate — perhaps female –from the Latin America-Caribbean region.” A UN diplomat said Friday that all seven hopefuls had received a vote of “discourage,” effectively a veto, from a permanent UN Security Council member in anonymous informal polling. Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan — who has been among the frontrunners in five previous polls — received the most “encourage” votes, but also got five “discourage” votes, including two from permanent members of the 15-country council. US media reports suggest Washington opposes all seven contenders. Among those considered by diplomats to be potential entrants are Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza under the US-backed “Board of Peace,” and the UAE’s minister of state for foreign affairs Lana Nusseibeh. Turkey’s Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, secretary general of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), has also had his name floated. The other candidates are Guyanese ex-foreign minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, Argentina’s Rafael Grossi, who heads the UN nuclear watchdog, Ecuador’s Ivonne A-Baki and Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Uganda’s Olara Otunnu. The outgoing secretary-general, Antonio Guterres of Portugal, ends his second five-year term on December 31. Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 in the Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided. items.title: Credit growth rose 34% to GH¢128.3 billion as of August 2026 – BoG
items.description: Credit growth accelerated sharply in the first eight months, with gross loans and advances rising 34.6% (GH¢32.96 billion) to GH¢128.3 billion by the end of August 2026. This is compared with 10.0% (GH¢32.96 billion) growth a year earlier. According to the September 2026 Monetary Policy Report, stronger lending to the private sector and a rebound in public sector credit drove the expansion. Consequently, the private sector’s share of total credit increased to 96.1% from 95.5%, highlighting the continued concentration of bank lending toward private sector activities. Credit to the public sector also increased over the same comparative period, growing by 16.1% in August 2026, compared to a contraction of 26.9% in the previous year. Sectoral Allocation The sectoral allocation of bank credit at end-August 2026 remained concentrated in a few key sectors of the economy. The services sector continued to receive the largest proportion of industry credit, representing 37.7% of total lending, which was higher than its share in the corresponding period of 2025. The commerce and finance sector followed with a share of 22.4%, while the construction sector recorded a notable increase, accounting for 11.3% of total credit. Collectively, these three sectors absorbed 71.3% of total industry lending, slightly below the 73.5% recorded a year earlier, indicating a modest diversification in the sectoral distribution of credit.

items.title: From passion to enterprise: Exzanita Aidoo journey into fashion entrepreneurship
items.description: In an era where entrepreneurship is increasingly becoming an attractive pathway for young people seeking financial independence, personal fulfilment and economic empowerment, the story of Exzanita Aidoo offers an interesting perspective on the power of passion, ambition and the courage to take the first step. For many young people, the dream of owning a business often remains just that, a dream. The fear of failure, limited access to capital, uncertainty about market opportunities and the comfort of regular employment frequently discourage them from pursuing their entrepreneurial ambitions. However, for Exzanita Aidoo, a young Ghanaian professional with experience working with Chanels Tradex, her passion for fashion has become the foundation for a new entrepreneurial journey. She is transforming a personal interest into a commercial venture through the establishment of an online fashion store and the launch of the CK Collection brand. Her journey reflects a growing movement among young Africans who are increasingly looking beyond traditional career paths to create businesses around their talents, interests and creative abilities. It tells the powerful story of how a young Ghanaian entrepreneur is turning her love for fashion into a growing business and inspiring a generation to pursue their dreams. A Passion that Inspired a Business Fashion has long been more than clothing. It is an expression of personality, identity, creativity and culture. For young entrepreneurs like Exzanita, it also represents an opportunity to create economic value. Her decision to establish an online fashion store and introduce the CK Collection brand demonstrates how an interest in style and fashion can provide the starting point for entrepreneurship. While many people admire fashion trends, follow designers and enjoy putting together attractive outfits, relatively few take the additional step of translating that enthusiasm into a business. That transition, from appreciating fashion as a consumer to participating in the industry as an entrepreneur, is an important aspect of Exzanita’s story. The creation of CK Collection represents her entry into a competitive industry where success requires much more than a good eye for fashion. Understanding customer preferences, identifying suitable products, developing a distinctive brand identity, managing finances and delivering excellent customer service are all essential to building a sustainable enterprise. For an emerging entrepreneur, these responsibilities present both challenges and opportunities for personal and professional growth. Building a Business while Developing a Career One of the interesting dimensions of Exzanita’s entrepreneurial journey is her professional experience with Chanels Tradex which provides an important context for understanding her decision to pursue entrepreneurship. For young professionals, employment can serve as a valuable platform for acquiring transferable skills, building networks, understanding workplace expectations and developing the discipline required to operate a business. Entrepreneurship does not necessarily require abandoning one’s professional career. In many instances, young people can begin by developing a business idea alongside their existing responsibilities, gradually building the experience, customer base and financial capacity required for expansion. This approach can help reduce some of the risks associated with starting a business, particularly in an economic environment where access to affordable financing remains a significant challenge. Exzanita’s move into fashion entrepreneurship therefore provides an opportunity to reflect on how young professionals can identify commercial opportunities beyond their primary occupations. Creating a Brand Beyond Clothing The establishment of CK Collection marks an important step in Exzanita’s ambition to build a presence in the fashion industry. In today’s increasingly competitive marketplace, launching a fashion business involves more than sourcing clothing and offering products for sale. Entrepreneurs must create a brand that customers can recognise, trust and associate with values. A successful fashion brand communicates an identity. It gives customers a reason to choose its products over competing alternatives and creates an emotional connection that goes beyond the transaction. For CK Collection, the opportunity lies in developing a distinctive market position, understanding the preferences of its target customers and consistently delivering value. The brand also enters the market at a time when digital platforms are changing how fashion businesses reach consumers. Social media, online marketplaces, mobile money services and digital advertising have significantly reduced some of the traditional barriers to entry, enabling emerging entrepreneurs to promote and sell products without necessarily investing in expensive physical retail spaces. For young Ghanaian entrepreneurs, these developments offer opportunities to test business ideas, engage directly with customers and gradually expand their operations. However, the accessibility of digital platforms should not be mistaken for a guarantee of commercial success. Online businesses must still overcome challenges relating to visibility, customer trust, product quality, logistics, competition and profitability. Building CK Collection into a sustainable business will therefore require continuous learning, strategic decisions and a willingness to adapt to changing market conditions. Turning Passion into Gains Perhaps the most important lesson from Exzanita’s journey is that passion can provide the motivation to start a business, but passion alone cannot sustain it. Many young people possess talents and interests in areas such as fashion, photography, music, beauty, food, technology, sports and creative arts. Yet, the ability to transform these interests into viable businesses requires a deliberate process. The first step is identifying a genuine market need. Loving fashion, for instance, does not automatically mean customers will purchase every product an entrepreneur offers. Successful businesses are built by understanding what people want, what they are willing to pay for and how their needs can be met better than existing alternatives. The second step involves starting with available resources. Contrary to popular perception, not every business requires substantial initial capital. Digital technology has created opportunities for young people to begin on a relatively small scale, validate demand and reinvest earnings into growth. An aspiring fashion entrepreneur might start with a carefully selected range of products, establish an online presence and use customer feedback to determine which offerings have the greatest commercial potential. The third step is developing basic business management skills. Financial discipline, record-keeping, pricing, inventory management, marketing and customer relations are essential, regardless of the size of the enterprise. Without these capabilities, even businesses built around exceptional talents can struggle to survive. Finally, aspiring entrepreneurs must recognise that building a successful business takes time. The excitement associated with launching a brand must be matched by patience, resilience and a commitment to continuous improvement. Lessons for the Next Generation There are several lessons that young people can draw from Exzanita’s decision to venture into fashion entrepreneurship. One is that meaningful business ideas can emerge from everyday interests. An individual does not necessarily need to discover an entirely new product or service to become an entrepreneur. Opportunities often exist in familiar industries where customers continue to seek quality, convenience, affordability and distinctive experiences. Another lesson is the importance of taking action. Many potentially successful businesses never move beyond the planning stage because their prospective founders continue waiting for perfect conditions. While careful preparation is necessary, entrepreneurship also requires the confidence to test ideas, learn from experience and make adjustments along the way. There is also a lesson about personal branding and differentiation. In an increasingly crowded digital marketplace, young entrepreneurs must consider what makes their businesses distinctive and why customers should develop lasting relationships with their brands. Equally important is the willingness to invest in learning. Whether through formal training, mentorship, industry events or practical experience, entrepreneurs must continuously strengthen their understanding of the markets in which they operate. Above all, young people must approach entrepreneurship with realistic expectations. Social media frequently celebrates the visible achievements of successful entrepreneurs while paying less attention to the financial uncertainty, operational difficulties and personal sacrifices involved in building a business. Sustainable entrepreneurship is not simply about launching a brand or generating online attention. It is about developing a business capable of creating value, satisfying customers and remaining financially viable over time. As her entrepreneurial journey unfolds, the ultimate measure of success will not merely be the visibility of the brand, but its ability to build customer trust, generate sustainable value and establish a lasting presence in the market.

items.title: Centre was compelled to impose emergency in KP, PM reiterates
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday reiterated that the Centre was “compelled” to impose emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa due to the provincial government’s lack of cooperation in countering terrorism. The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament this week amid protests by the opposition. On Saturday, PM Shehbaz visited the residence of Rashid Bashir Virk in Gujranwala to offer condolences on the demise of his father, late MNA Mahmood Bashir Virk . After recalling the late PML-N lawmaker’s services, the premier stressed that the Centre was compelled to impose emergency in KP. He said the Centre made a “last attempt”, referring to the rounds of talks held by a joint delegation of the PPP and the government with the opposition. The hours-long second round, held on Oct 3 , had ended without a breakthrough . “They had talks with them (PTI) day and night, for 48 hours, and sat with the intention to settle matters from every aspect,” PM Shehbaz said, adding that a draft was ready under which the PTI was to call off its long march. The prime minister highlighted that he had held multiple meetings with Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role now stands non-functional, as well as with his predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur . “In every meeting, I tried my best to convey to him from the depths of my heart and with seriousness that KP is an extremely beautiful province and has very brave and honourable people, […] and I am always present in every way for their development and prosperity,” PM Shehbaz said. The premier added that he assured the KP government of the Centre’s support in fighting against terrorism together to face the security challenges in the province. PM Shehbaz said he had assured the chief minister that he would make the decisions regarding the administration, resources and necessities in consultation with him. “But, unfortunately, despite all these efforts, thousands of our law enforcement agencies personnel, soldiers, officers and officers of the armed forces were sacrificing their lives every day to defend the homeland.” The prime minister stressed that the federal government “made many efforts” regarding the situation, but there were “threats and long marches every other day in response”. “Their past history is very horrific,” he remarked, recalling the 2014 sit-ins staged by the PTI at Islamabad’s D-Chowk during the tenure of his brother, Nawaz Sharif. “Last year as well, you saw how the entire country was jammed by staging a sit-in in Islamabad,” he added, ostensibly referring to the PTI’s November 2024 protest that had resulted in clashes. “This time as well, they had an entire plan of bloodshed,” he alleged. The Oct 11 imposition of emergency and governor’s rule followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Federal ministers alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups and asserted that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there. The Centre and the PTI have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their October 3 talks . The PTI said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre denied . It also called for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticised the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objected to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

items.title: États-Unis : la nouvelle porte-parole de Trump quitte déjà la Maison Blanche cinq jours après sa nomination
items.description: Cinq jours seulement apres sa prise de fonctions, la porte-parole de la Maison Blanche, Katie Zacharia, a quitte son poste le 16 octobre. L'administration de Donald Trump a confirme son depart, annoncant qu'elle devrait occuper un autre poste, encore non precise. Aucun successeur n'a ete designe. Choisie pour remplacer Karoline Leavitt, partie en août, Katie Zacharia etait connue comme commentatrice conservatrice sur Fox News et Newsmax. Elle avait aussi travaille comme conseillere en communication chez Trump Media & Technology Group, proprietaire du reseau Truth Social. Des le 13 octobre, son premier briefing a toutefois suscite des critiques. En 14 minutes, dont environ cinq consacrees aux questions, elle n'a donne la parole qu'a trois journalistes, de Breitbart, de Fox News et du Daily Mail . Elle a notamment annonce que Donald Trump avait demande la demission de Kimberly Guilfoyle, ambassadrice americaine en Grece. Cette intervention restera la seule de son mandat. Face aux critiques, Katie Zacharia a explique avoir recu ses derniers documents moins de deux heures avant le briefing, apres une nomination organisee dans l'urgence. Des qualifications juridiques au cœur de la polemique a cette prestation contestee s'est ajoutee une polemique sur ses qualifications juridiques, Katie Zacharia ayant echoue a l'examen du barreau de Californie, alors qu'elle se presentait publiquement comme avocate. Diplomee de l'universite Pepperdine en 2011, elle a reconnu cet echec, expliquant que le resultat lui importait peu puisqu'elle s'appretait a rejoindre son mari en Chine. Elle ne disposait d'aucune licence l'autorisant a exercer le droit aux etats-Unis. Si une telle licence n'est pas necessaire pour etre porte-parole, l'utilisation du titre d'avocate a souleve des questions. L'organisation Campaign for Accountability a ainsi depose une plainte aupres du barreau californien pour demander un examen de sa situation. Les critiques sont venues jusque des medias proches de Donald Trump. Le presentateur de Fox News et allie du president, Sean Hannity, a interroge Katie Zacharia avec insistance sur son briefing et ses qualifications. Meme sur une chaîne habituellement favorable a la Maison Blanche, les explications de la nouvelle porte-parole n'ont donc pas echappe aux questions embarrassantes. Du soutien enthousiaste au depart express Le directeur de la communication de la Maison Blanche, Steven Cheung, promettait pourtant a Katie Zacharia une place parmi les grandes figures de la communication de l'administration Trump. Deux jours plus tard, son passage a ce poste prenait deja fin. Donald Trump a lui-meme laisse entendre le 16 octobre que cette fonction ne convenait peut-etre pas a sa porte-parole. Il lui avait conseille de « reconsiderer » sa decision, tout en denoncant le traitement particulierement severe que les medias lui avaient, selon lui, reserve. Apres la confirmation de son depart, Katie Zacharia a neanmoins rendu un hommage appuye au president americain sur X, le decrivant comme un homme « gentil, merveilleux, genereux, attentionne, enthousiaste et travailleur ». Avec cinq jours en poste, elle etablit le record du mandat le plus court pour une porte-parole de la Maison Blanche. Meme Anthony Scaramucci, ancien directeur de la communication de Donald Trump, avait tenu plus longtemps, avec 11 jours en fonction en 2017. « Les records sont faits pour etre battus. Mais je ne prends aucun plaisir a la souffrance des autres », a-t-il ironise sur X. Ce depart intervient a moins de trois semaines des elections de mi-mandat, alors que Donald Trump a lui-meme deplore les difficultes de communication de son administration. Malgre cette nouvelle vacance a un poste cle, le president americain ne serait toujours pas presse de designer une remplacante.

items.title: 2027: We’ll defeat Tinubu in 12 states – Makinde’s campaign
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, MDPCO, has vowed that its candidate, Seyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, will defeat President Bola Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the President, including Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Abuja, in the January 2027 presidential election. The campaign organisation said Tinubu’s planned visits to the states would do little to change what it described as growing opposition to his re-election, blaming the hardship Nigerians face on his administration’s policies and accusing members of his inner circle of aggravating public resentment through political arrogance. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Hon. Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO said Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA agenda was gaining traction across the country, particularly among young people, and challenged Tinubu to test his popularity through direct engagement with voters rather than campaign rallies. The organisation listed Oyo, Kaduna, Rivers, Plateau, Borno, Enugu, Bauchi, Sokoto, Delta, Kano, Adamawa and Lagos as the 12 states Tinubu had identified for personal campaign visits, claiming the move reflected concern over Makinde’s growing political foothold. “Mr. President should know that his visit to these states, if he eventually does, will not in any way change the direction or the determination of the people to vote him out,” the statement said. The campaign challenged Tinubu to travel by road through the states and see for himself the condition of federal highways, the living conditions of Nigerians and the state of public infrastructure. “We challenge President Tinubu not to have a change of mind but visit the states to face the people. He should travel around the country by road and witness the decrepit state of federal highways, the squalor in which Nigerians live and the level of infrastructural decay across the country,” it said. The MDPCO accused the administration of spending trillions of naira on wasteful programmes and projects while Nigerians grapple with economic hardship. It also dismissed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda as ineffective, arguing that Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA programme offered a more practical alternative. The proposed agenda, according to the organisation, centres on an inclusive, four-year transitional government of national unity, with education, the economy, security and socio-political reforms as its four priority areas. It said Makinde’s economic plan would tackle poverty through increased production, while his security strategy would combine intelligence gathering, social reorientation and kinetic and non-kinetic measures. The education component would expand access to quality, functional education, while institutional reforms would promote inclusive governance and responsible leadership. The campaign said feedback from its field operations showed that the RESET NIGERIA message was resonating with Nigerians, especially young people, whom it claimed were looking to Makinde for an alternative to the current administration. It urged Tinubu not to waste national resources on what it called his “Nebuchadnezzar” campaign council, dismissing its members as failed politicians unable to attract votes. The MDPCO maintained that neither the President’s campaign machinery nor the use of incumbency would reverse what it described as a growing electoral backlash, insisting that Makinde would defeat Tinubu in the battleground states and across the federation. items.title: Mobilisation du 17 octobre : des milliers de manifestants en région, vives tensions à Paris et Marseille
items.description: La tension a grimpé fortement à Paris samedi avant même le départ du défilé place de la République, comme à Marseille, avec une intrusion dans la mairie, à l'occasion de la journée de mobilisation nationale contre la « vie chère » qui a rassemblé plus de 30.000 personnes en région dans la matinée. « A la mi-journée » , les autorités ont recensé 140 actions avec 32.800 personnes en province et 166 interpellations sur tout le territoire national, a annoncé l'entourage du ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez dans un message à la presse. Au même moment, de vives tensions entre manifestants et forces de l'ordre éclataient à Paris, place de la République, d'où doit partir vers 14H00 un cortège protéiforme. Les forces de l'ordre ont fait usage à plusieurs reprises de gaz lacrymogènes pour répondre à plusieurs centaines de manifestants, pour la plupart masqués et vêtus de noir, dont certains tiraient des mortiers d'artifice. Toute la matinée, des contrôles stricts ont été réalisés dans la capitale pour faire respecter les arrêtés d'interdiction de manifester dans certains secteurs de la capitale et pour intervenir autour de plusieurs cortèges sauvages. Une vingtaine d'interpellations ont eu lieu après une action devant le siège de CNews à Paris. Des projectiles ont été lancés et des vitres brisées, entraînant l'intervention des forces de l'ordre pour disperser les individus, selon la préfecture de police. À Marseille, Lyon, Niort, Valenciennes ou La Rochelle, des manifestants – certains avec des gilets jaunes – avaient lancé samedi matin dans les rues une mobilisation comprenant de multiples inconnues, apparues sur les réseaux sociaux avant d'être nourrie par les « colères » de gilets jaunes, des lycéens et étudiants, de salariés ou de militants pour le climat. Le tout sous la surveillance étroite de forces de l'ordre déployées en nombre. Un bâtiment de la fac de lettres de Rouen a notamment été touché tôt samedi par un incendie vraisemblablement d' « origine criminelle » , selon une source proche du dossier. À Marseille, « sur la Canebière, des magasins ont été vandalisés et le poste de police municipale a été dégradé », selon l'entourage du ministre de l'Intérieur. Des manifestants ont également pénétré dans le hall de la mairie après avoir enfoncé la porte, selon un journaliste de l'AFP. © AFP On étouffe Peu de blocages ont été constatés par les journalistes de l'AFP, avec néanmoins quelques ronds-points occupés à Rennes, Langon (Gironde) ou Marmande (Lot-et-Garonne), en écho au mouvement historique des gilets jaunes en 2018-2019. A Toulouse, les forces de l'ordre sont intervenues pour empêcher des blocages de trains et d'un rond-point. Sur le site 17octobregiletjaune.net, l'appel à la mobilisation s'adresse également aux habitants des quartiers, paysans, ouvriers ou retraités, invités à descendre dans la rue et sur des ronds-points ou autour de stations-services, de péages ou d'axes de circulation. À six mois de l'élection présidentielle, l'appel à faire renaître le mouvement des gilets jaunes, qui avait marqué le premier mandat d'Emmanuel Macron, a rencontré la protestation des lycéens et étudiants pour de meilleures conditions d'études. « À la fin du mois, je n'ai plus rien, les prix augmentent mais pas les salaires. On n'en peut plus, on étouffe », dénonce Franck, un fonctionnaire quadragénaire qui a manifesté à Guéret avec environ 400 personnes. L'ampleur de la mobilisation était une grande inconnue de cette journée, au premier jour des vacances scolaires et alors qu'une intersyndicale a appelé les salariés du public et du privé à manifester et faire grève le 5 novembre, notamment pour les salaires et les services publics. © AFP Macron appelle au « calme » – Emmanuel Macron avait lancé vendredi, depuis Bruxelles, un appel « au calme ». Mais Beauvau n'avait pas caché sa crainte de « débordements (…) dans les cortèges notamment parisiens et dans les grandes villes ». « La probabilité que l'ultragauche fasse dégénérer les cortèges de l'après-midi (de samedi) est très forte », a jugé samedi midi l'entourage du ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez, en dénonçant des « opérations violentes et ciblées » dans certains endroits en France. Cette source a souligné que « le mouvement se tradui(sait) par une très forte mobilisation de la mouvance ultragauche, qui ne cherche qu'à créer le désordre ». Ces derniers jours, le gouvernement avait tenté de désamorcer le mécontentement de certaines couches de la population : enveloppe de 500 et 700 millions d'euros débloquée pour le plan de relance agricole pour 2027, alors que le spectre d'une mobilisation des agriculteurs a ressurgi, prolongation d'aides à l'achat de carburants. Côté politique, de nombreux députés LFI, écolos et du Parti communiste sont attendus. « Revoir » sa doctrine du maintien de l'ordre © AFP La cheffe des écologistes et candidate à la présidentielle Marine Tondelier a appelé le gouvernement à « revoir » sa doctrine du maintien de l'ordre, qui met en danger « manifestants et policiers » , alors que les tensions se prolongent en marge de plusieurs cortèges en France. « J'en ai ras-le-bol de la doctrine de maintien de l'ordre dans ce pays. Il faut la revoir et vite, parce que ça finit par être une atteinte aux atteintes. Et en plus, ça met tout le monde en danger, les manifestants et les policiers », a déclaré Tondelier depuis le rassemblement de la place de la République à Paris où ont éclaté des affrontements entre forces de l'ordre public et manifestants avant même le début de la manifestation. The post Mobilisation du 17 octobre : des milliers de manifestants en région, vives tensions à Paris et Marseille appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion — Makinde
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country. Makinde said Christians could not afford to stand aloof from politics on the grounds that it was dirty or that they should not serve under leaders who did not share their faith, stressing that national transformation required their active participation. He spoke on Saturday in Abuja after receiving a Christian Icon Award at the Christian Association of Nigeria’s (CAN) 50th anniversary celebration. The governor, who is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), said Christians should draw lessons from biblical figures who accepted difficult assignments in pursuit of a greater purpose. “It is typical for us to say, ‘Politics is dirty. I don’t want to be yoked with unbelievers’, and things like that. But we must look at biblical examples,” he said. Makinde cited David, who, despite having been anointed king, served in the palace of Saul, from whom God had departed. He said the biblical account should challenge Christians who believe they cannot serve under leaders of different religious persuasions. “I will use this opportunity to encourage our Christian brothers and sisters across the country to rise up and participate in the agenda to transform Nigeria and reset our country,” he said. Makinde urged Christians to focus on the hardship confronting Nigerians rather than allowing religious differences to define their engagement with national affairs. “Our problem is not primarily a religious one. Our problem in this country is poverty — grinding poverty,” he said. “At this stage, we must focus on addressing the issues currently confronting us. Those are the challenges we need to tackle.” The post Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion — Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Sérénité et détermination dans les centres d'examen de Kankan. Ce samedi matin, au lycée Morifindjan Diabaté, les candidats au concours de recrutement des enseignants ont rejoint leurs salles dans le calme, affichant une confiance intacte malgré le déséquilibre entre le nombre de postulants et les places mises en compétition par le Gouvernement. L'ambiance est studieuse et empreinte d'espoir. Dans les différentes salles du lycée Morifindian Diabaté, centre retenu pour les épreuves, les candidats au concours de recrutement des enseignants se disent prêts. Malgré la forte affluence observée dès les premières heures, le mot d'ordre est à la sérénité. C'est le cas de Mohamed Lamine Barry, rencontré à quelques minutes du démarrage des épreuves. « Nous abordons les épreuves avec confiance. Nous sommes très confiants, même si nous savons que le nombre de postulants est très élevé par rapport au nombre demandé par le gouvernement », confie-t-il. Pour lui, les consignes sont claires. La fiche d'évaluation, jugée accessible, et la vidéo explicative publiée par le ministère de la Modernisation de l'Administration et de la Fonction publique ont permis de lever les dernières interrogations. « Nous avons très bien compris. La fiche d'évaluation est vraiment simple et compréhensible. Il y a déjà une vidéo publiée par le ministère que nous avons regardée. Ce matin, ils ont également renforcé ces explications », rassure-t-il. Patience et espoir dans les salles Dans les salles, l'attente est palpable mais calme. Les candidats, concentrés, espèrent voir leurs efforts récompensés. Finda Suzane Bongono, candidate présente dans l'une des salles, dit attendre les épreuves avec patience et sérénité, tout en souhaitant bonne chance à l'ensemble des compétiteurs. « Je suis à 100% confiant » Pour beaucoup, ce concours est plus qu'une simple évaluation. C'est l'espoir d'une stabilisation professionnelle après des années de précarité. C'est le sentiment de Raphaël Bongono, enseignant contractuel communautaire venu de Mandiana (zone 4). Pour lui, l'expérience du terrain est un atout majeur. « Mon état d'esprit est positif. Je suis prêt à affronter n'importe quelle question qu'on va me soumettre », affirme-t-il avec assurance. « Après plusieurs années de chômage, nous sommes là. Nous sommes prêts à affronter. Et nous allons toujours continuer à chercher, à nous battre pour atteindre notre objectif. » Interrogé sur son niveau de confiance, il ne tergiverse pas : « Je suis à 100%. Ainsi que tous mes amis, c'est à 100%. » Il rappelle le sacrifice consenti par les contractuels communautaires : « Nous avons accepté d'aller dans les zones les plus lointaines de ce pays pour relever les défis. Pour cela, nous nous en remettons à Dieu. » Au-delà de la compétition, ce concours est perçu à Kankan comme une véritable bouffée d'oxygène pour des centaines d'enseignants qui aspirent à intégrer définitivement la Fonction publique. Les épreuves n'attendent plus que le top départ. Karifa Kansan Doumbouya, correspondant régional – Kankan L’article Concours de la Fonction publique à Kankan : des candidats enseignants confiants malgré la forte concurrence est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
