items.title: Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair enters Day 2 in Ho
items.description: Day Two of the Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair is underway at the Ho Sports Stadium in the Volta Region, bringing together businesses in the housing and construction sectors to showcase products and services to prospective homeowners and other visitors. The three-day fair, which began on Friday, October 16, is expected to run until Sunday, October 18, providing a platform for exhibitors to engage the public on housing solutions, building materials, property development and home improvement. The event is organised by Republic Bank in partnership with JoyNews. Participating companies and institutions are displaying a range of products and services, offering visitors the opportunity to interact directly with industry players, make enquiries and explore options for building, buying or improving their homes. Exhibitors at the fair include Republic Bank, DoorMaster, Virtual Security Africa, Ayuda Hub Limited, Sintex Tanks, Nestas Homes Limited, Adonai Estate Limited, MTN, C Techi GH Limited, Waylead Company GH Ltd, Akwaaba Building Materials, Interplast, Rhoyak Ventures, Simef Gold Limited, Lesh Fortune Ltd, Lipe Builders & Contractors, Vol-link Roofing System and TDC Ghana Ltd. Their presence reflects the range of services and products available across the housing value chain, from financing and property development to building materials, roofing systems, water storage and security solutions. The fair offers prospective homeowners an opportunity to learn more about available products, compare options and engage businesses on their specific housing needs. It also creates a space for participating companies to showcase their offerings, interact with potential customers and strengthen their visibility in the Volta Region. On the first day, visitors continued to attend the fair despite light showers, with exhibitors maintaining their presence as the event progressed. The second day is expected to provide further opportunities for members of the public to explore the exhibition stands, seek information from participating businesses and engage with service providers in the housing and construction industries. The fair continues on Saturday, October 17, and Sunday, October 18, at the Ho Sports Stadium. Members of the public interested in housing, property development, construction materials, and home improvement are encouraged to visit the venue and engage with the exhibitors.

items.title: Secrétaire général des Nations Unies : Macky Sall retire sa candidature
items.description: L’ancien président de la République du Sénégal, Macky Sall, a annoncé samedi le retrait de sa candidature au poste de Secrétaire général des Nations Unies. L’information a été donnée à travers un communiqué de presse. Le prédécesseur du chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, ne sera plus dans la course pour le poste de Secrétaire général des Nations Unies. Macky Sall a décidé samedi de retirer sa candidature. « A l'issue du vote informel du 16 octobre 2026 pour l'élection au poste de Secrétaire général des Nations Unies, et après consultations avec Evariste Ndayishimiye, président de la République du Burundi, Président en exercice de l'Union Africaine, et Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, Président de la République du Sénégal, Président en exercice de la CEDEAO, j'ai décidé de retirer ma candidature audit poste », a-t-il écrit à travers un communiqué de presse. En réalité, l’ancien président de la République du Sénégal explique qu’il a pris cette décision avec un « profond sens des responsabilités », en espérant contribuer ainsi à l'émergence d'une candidature consensuelle au sein du Conseil de sécurité. Mais aussi, en gardant à l'esprit que depuis le début du processus, les résultats des différents votes tests indiquent un choix en faveur d'une candidature issue de la région d'Amérique latine et des Caraïbes, et éventuellement féminine. A lire aussi : Secrétariat général ONU : le président B. D. Faye renouvelle son soutien à la candidature de Macky Sall « Pour ma part, ma candidature était essentiellement motivée par la volonté de mettre mon expérience de près de quarante ans de vie publique au service des Nations Unies. Je tiens à remercier le président Evariste Ndayishimiye, qui a parrainé ma candidature, et le président Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, qui l'a soutenue », a-t-il ajouté. Alors que le monde reste confronté à la multiplication des conflits, à l'aggravation des rivalités géopolitiques, à la fragmentation de l'ordre international et à des défis économiques et financiers sans précédent, Macky Sall demeure convaincu que les Nations Unies doivent engager une transformation profonde de leurs méthodes de travail et de leur fonctionnement. Et, selon lui, l'Afrique, qui est au cœur des enjeux de paix, de sécurité et de développement, doit aussi continuer à faire entendre sa voix et poursuivre ses efforts afin d'occuper la place qui lui revient dans la gouvernance mondiale. « Je retire ma candidature, mais reste pleinement engagé au service des idéaux qui l'ont inspirée : la paix, la sécurité, le développement économique et social, la coopération internationale et le dialogue entre les nations. Je souhaite plein succès à la personne qui sera appelée à exercer les hautes responsabilités de Secrétaire général des Nations Unies », a-t-il conclu. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Exportations : l’automobile en tête au Maroc avec 159,2 MMDH en 2025
items.description: Le secteur automobile a maintenu en 2025 sa place de premier secteur exportateur pour la troisième année consécutive, avec des exportations atteignant 159,2 milliards de dirhams (MMDH), selon l'Office des Changes. Ces exportations enregistrent une légère baisse par rapport à 2024 (159,6 MMDH), précise l'Office dans son rapport annuel sur le Commerce extérieur du Maroc. Ce recul est dû à une diminution des ventes de l'écosystème construction (-9,6 MMDH ou -13,5%), atténuée par la hausse des exportations de l'écosystème câblage (+5 MMDH ou +9%) et de l'écosystème intérieur véhicules et sièges (+1,1 MMDH ou +11,5%). D'après la même source, les phosphates et dérivés se placent au deuxième rang des secteurs exportateurs avec 99,7 MMDH, en progression de 14,5%. La hausse concerne tous les produits : les engrais naturels et chimiques (+14,1%), l'acide phosphorique (+14,8%) et les phosphates (+17,3%). De leur part, les exportations du secteur agriculture et agro-alimentaire atteignent 87,5 MMDH, en légère hausse (+0,5 MMDH) suite à l'augmentation des ventes de l'agriculture, sylviculture et chasse (+2,1 MMDH), atténuée en partie par la baisse des ventes de l'industrie alimentaire (-1,5 MMDH). Les exportations du secteur aéronautique enregistrent une hausse de 2,7 MMDH ou +9,8%, liée essentiellement à l'accroissement des ventes de l'écosystème assemblage (+1,9 MMDH ou +10,6%). En revanche, les exportations du secteur textile et cuir baissent de 2,1 MMDH ou -4,6%, passant de 45,9 MMDH en 2024 à 43,7 MMDH en 2025. Celles du secteur électronique et électricité reculent également, en raison notamment de la baisse des exportations des composants électroniques (transistors) de 3 MMDH ou -38,8%. Globalement, les exportations du Maroc progressent de 3% à 470 MMDH en 2025. Par produits, les engrais naturels et chimiques se classent en tête avec une part de 15,6%, suivis des voitures de tourisme (12,6%) et des fils, câbles et autres conducteurs isolés pour l'électricité (11,9%). The post Exportations : l’automobile en tête au Maroc avec 159,2 MMDH en 2025 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

Affi Agbenyo has no business being Deputy EC Chair based on NDC’s espoused principles – Akosua Manu
items.description: Adviser on Gender and Social Protection to former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Akosua Manu, has criticised the appointment of Affi Agbenyo as Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC), saying that it contradicts principles previously advanced by the National Democratic Congress (NDC). She said the NDC had strongly opposed the appointment of individuals it considered politically affiliated to the EC under the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) government, raising concerns about their ability to remain impartial. Speaking on JoyNews ’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, Ms Manu said the same standard should apply to the current government following the appointment and swearing-in of two new Deputy Chairpersons. “Based on the NDC’s own principles, Affi Agbenyo has no business being Deputy EC Chair,” she said. Ms Manu said that the NDC had previously described the appointment of former EC Chairperson Jean Mensa in strong terms, including as “indecent” and “a gross abuse of discretionary powers”, because of concerns about her perceived political affiliations. She questioned why the party appeared to have adopted a different position after returning to power. “If I should take reactions to Madam Jean Mensa’s appointment at the time, these were the adjectives ascribed to her appointment: indecent, a gross abuse of discretionary powers, regrettable, silly, but to name a few,” she said. Ms Manu also referred to comments made by President John Mahama in May 2024, when he criticised former President Nana Akufo-Addo’s appointments to the Electoral Commission. According to her, Mahama had raised concerns about politically exposed individuals and people allegedly associated with the NPP’s Tertiary Students Confederacy Network (TESCON) being appointed to the Commission. She said the President’s earlier position appeared inconsistent with the appointment of Ms Agbenyo. Ms Manu cited remarks Mr Mahama reportedly made during the swearing-in of the new EC Chairpersons, in which he urged the officials to serve the country without political bias. “Your duty is to the Republic of Ghana and its people,” the President said, according to the quotation cited by Ms Manu. She said the President had also urged the new EC officials to uphold fairness and transparency and apply the law without fear or favour towards any political party or government. Ms Manu questioned what had changed in less than two years to justify the appointment of someone who’s a known NDC activist. “In less than two years, when he was very clear in his mind that anybody affiliated to our party allegedly should have no business being a deputy chair or a chair at the EC, what has changed?” she asked. She insisted that the issue was not simply whether the appointee was a party member, but whether her political activities raised legitimate questions about her ability to serve independently. “The lady in question is not just a member, as they are trying to portray here. She’s actually an activist. There are videos, the platforms she mounted. There is work she did with them,” she said. Ms Manu rejected suggestions that the NDC could defend the appointment by saying that the previous NPP government had also appointed people accused of having political affiliations. She said the NDC had presented itself as committed to correcting what it considered improper appointments under the previous administration. According to her, the party should therefore be judged by the standards it established while in opposition. “If the principle is that you honestly do believe that anybody affiliated to a political party has no business sharing this high office and that you believe that they’ll be impartial, and you have once described that connection as indecent and a gross abuse of discretionary powers, then the chickens have come home to roost,” she said. Responding to suggestions that the current government was merely following the precedent set by the NPP, Ms Manu said such an argument would undermine the NDC’s promise to reset public institutions. “In the reset that they promised, where everything that we did was unconscionable and was wrong, and they, in their reset agenda, were to right the wrongs, is writing the wrong now, doing the same things that you said were improper?” she asked. “I think it’s dishonest. It’s literally an insult to the intelligence of Ghanaians,” she added. Ms Manu also questioned the advice and consultations that preceded the appointments, particularly the role played by the Council of State. She said she had not seen a clear account of the Council’s position on the appointments and called for greater clarity on the process. “I believe that the Council of State weighs in on such appointments. What was their take on this? I’ve not seen it,” she said. During the discussion, Ms Manu was asked whether her argument meant she now regretted the appointment of Dr Peter Appiahene, a former EC member whose appointment under the previous NPP administration attracted criticism over alleged political affiliations. She said she did not regret the appointment of a competent person, but said that the broader issue was the apparent inconsistency in the NDC’s position. “I do not regret a competent person being put in a position. What I regret is that within two years of seeing that the people who mounted a defence and who criticised a party sympathiser…” she said. “So the regret is that Ghanaians believed in that principled position, only for them to renege on that. That is what should be in question, not my position on what happened a couple of years ago,” she said.

items.title: Recrutement de 6 000 enseignants : forte mobilisation des candidats à Kindia
items.description: Les épreuves du concours de recrutement de 6 000 agents pour le secteur de l’enseignement ont été officiellement lancées en République de Guinée. Dans la préfecture de Kindia, près de 14 000 candidats prennent part aux épreuves, répartis dans 31 centres. a cérémonie officielle de lancement s’est déroulée au collège Tafory, sous la présidence du secrétaire général du ministère de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique. À l’occasion de cette cérémonie, le représentant du ministère a exprimé sa satisfaction quant à la forte mobilisation des candidats à Kindia, tout en saluant la tenue du concours à l’intérieur du pays. « C’est un sentiment de satisfaction qui m’anime ce matin en venant à Kindia, qui reçoit le plus grand nombre de candidats. Cela traduit toute la vision du président de la République, Son Excellence Mamadi Doumbouya, celle de permettre à notre ministère d’organiser le concours à l’intérieur du pays. Dans les sept régions, les concours se déroulent. Sur les 39 000 candidats pour 6 000 postes d’enseignants, près de 14 000 sont à Kindia. Il est donc important de venir visiter quelques centres et de voir comment les choses se passent. Dans les différentes salles, j’ai été particulièrement marqué par la forte participation des femmes. Cela traduit également la vision du président de la République, celle de dédier son mandat aux femmes. Nous sommes venus leur souhaiter bonne chance et constater que les épreuves sont bien distribuées et que toutes les dispositions sécuritaires sont prises. C’est aussi l’occasion de remercier les autorités locales et toutes les personnes mobilisées pour que ces épreuves se déroulent dans les meilleures conditions », a déclaré N’Faly Sylla, secrétaire général du ministère de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique. Les autorités entendent faire de ce concours un processus transparent, avec une politique de tolérance zéro face à la fraude et à la corruption. À cet effet, un dispositif de signalement a été mis en place en collaboration avec l’Agence nationale de sécurité des systèmes d’information « On veut une tolérance zéro face à la fraude. Nous avons mis en place un dispositif avec le numéro 1017 pour permettre de signaler les cas de fraude, en collaboration avec l’Agence nationale de sécurité des systèmes d’information. Pour tout signalement, nous invitons les citoyens à se rendre sur la plateforme Alerte.gov.gn ou à appeler le numéro indiqué. Les cas seront recensés et transmis aux autorités compétentes afin que les mesures nécessaires soient prises », a précisé l’émissaire du ministère. Du côté des candidats, les épreuves se déroulent dans un climat de sérénité. Chacun espère décrocher une place parmi les 6 000 postes mis en compétition. Interrogée sur le déroulement des épreuves, Aminata Hélène Camara s’est montrée satisfaite des premières étapes du processus. « Le concours a bien débuté. Il y a eu l’accueil des candidats, leur installation et maintenant, nous sommes à l’étape des épreuves », a-t-elle indiqué. À l’issue du concours, les copies seront acheminées vers un centre sécurisé à Conakry pour y être corrigées à l’aide d’un correcteur optique. Les résultats seront ensuite mis à la disposition des candidats. Aboubacar Dramé, correspondant régional à Kindia +224 623 08 09 10 L’article Recrutement de 6 000 enseignants : forte mobilisation des candidats à Kindia est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Another Battle Between the Catholic Church and the Trump Administration
items.description: Several winters ago, a few weeks before Christmas, I went to confession. The parish close to work was hosting a reconciliation service, meant to prepare the faithful to celebrate the birth of Christ. A dozen or so priests were scattered across the cathedral. Penitents lined the aisles. Whispers of contrition and pardon filled the air. The Catholic Church counsels believers to seek confession regularly—at the very least, once a year. I hadn’t been back in a few. So in addition to feeling spiritually unmoored, I was worried about how the priest would react to hearing about my hiatus. But when I told him, he simply smiled and said, “Welcome back.” His response put me at ease then, and it helped change how I approach the sacrament now: less as a nerve-racking ordeal, more as a moment of mercy. Sacraments such as confession are central to Catholicism. Through them, the Church teaches that simple actions—having a conversation with a priest, eating bread and drinking wine—are, with grace, tangible encounters with God. For the past year, the Trump administration has been making it harder for Catholics at migrant-detention centers to have those encounters. The most recent example came to light this month, when the Archdiocese of St. Louis filed a federal lawsuit over the visitation policy at Saint Genevieve County Jail in eastern Missouri. According to the claim, the 10 priests who minister at the jail aren’t allowed to celebrate Mass. The suit also alleges that priests are permitted to visit migrant detainees just once a week, during a four-hour period, and that the jail’s “no contact” security policy lets the clergy speak with detainees only over the phone, through a glass partition. As a result, the approximately 150 migrants at the jail at a given time—most of whom are Catholic, according to the archdiocese—have been going without their religious needs for weeks. Since the middle of 2025, according to the lawsuit, Saint Genevieve has housed approximately 3,000 people. [ Read: The Catholic Church’s new schism ] This isn’t the first time that Catholic clergy have complained that the government is preventing them from ministering to detained migrants. Last year, the Florida detention facility known as “Alligator Alcatraz” kept priests from visiting or offering Mass to detainees for a month, until an agreement was reached between the Archdiocese of Miami and state authorities. In May, after a six-month legal fight, a Catholic nonprofit won a preliminary injunction to let Catholic priests celebrate Mass and administer sacraments at the Broadview ICE processing center outside Chicago. And the administration’s immigration crackdowns seem to be hurting the Church more broadly. Dioceses across the country have reported decreased Mass attendance among Spanish-speaking parishioners who fear detention. ICE has reportedly conducted raids near Catholic churches during Mass hours. The Department of Homeland Security has denied allegations of wrongdoing at Saint Genevieve. In a statement to multiple outlets, the agency said that the jail is not an ICE facility—although Saint Genevieve is listed as a detention facility on ICE’s website —and that it “ensures detainees are accommodated with religious services.” As described in the lawsuit, however, those accommodations disregard the religious significance of the Catholic sacraments. Consider confession. The suit claims that at Saint Genevieve, conversations between detainees and priests are not private, and the phone lines that they use to talk may be monitored. These policies may be in place for security reasons, but confession is meant to be a private exchange between penitent and priest, who acts in persona Christi —in the person of Christ. Confession is “one of the most intimate, profound acts that someone can do,” David Inczauskis, a Jesuit priest who ministers at the Broadview ICE facility, told me. He added, “To state very specifically the sins that they have committed and to ask humbly for pardon and for peace” requires a “level of vulnerability” that is “very high.” An even bigger problem comes up with the sacrament of the Eucharist, or Communion. The complaint includes an email from a deputy at the local sheriff’s office suggesting that priests “provide an unopened, individually wrapped Communion wafer” to a member of the detention center staff, who could then hand it to a detainee. This way of distributing the Eucharist would be “sacrilegious,” as Archbishop Mitchell Rozanski of St. Louis recently told Reuters . The Church teaches that the Eucharist is the “Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity” of Christ—not a symbol, but God’s real presence . For that reason, Inczauskis said, the Church distributes the Eucharist through either ordained ministers or specially trained laypeople. [ Read: The Catholic Church and the Trump administration are not getting along ] For much of the past quarter century, many conservative figures have taken up religious liberty as an essential cause. The Trump administration purported to continue these efforts when it established a commission last year meant to identify “emerging threats” to the exercise of faith. In June, the commission released a draft report claiming that “in recent years, Americans from all religious backgrounds have faced increasing persecution for their religious beliefs.” Some of the issues discussed in the report include rising anti-Semitism, how gender and sexuality is taught in schools, and conscience protections for health-care workers who object to participating in abortions or assisted suicides. The report said nothing about the administration’s migrant-detention practices. When the commission was announced, my colleague Elizabeth Bruenig wrote that “Christians shouldn’t conclude” that it would “necessarily defend their interests.” That warning seems prescient a year and a half later. At Alligator Alcatraz, Broadview, and Saint Genevieve, the Catholic Church has shown that it believes that detainee access to the sacraments matters deeply. Given the choice between restricting immigration and protecting the religious liberty of migrants, the administration, too, has demonstrated where its values lie.

items.title: The Flying Car Must Never Be Built
items.description: Elon Musk revealed, in a dramatic demonstration on Thursday night at SpaceX’s rocket-testing facility near Waco, Texas, a new “flying” Tesla Roadster prototype. The car hung upside down on a curved track, then performed aerial stunts—including jumping over a Tesla semi, Evel Knievel–style—using air-powered thrusters designed in collaboration with SpaceX. The demo was impressive despite Musk’s awkward manner, which in the context of a supposed literal flying car came off as nerdy charm. After revealing the car, Musk paraphrased a quote from Peter Thiel, his former PayPal partner: “We wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters.” The line, which was part of a 2011 “manifesto” published by Thiel’s venture-capital firm Founders Fund, was intended to indict the feeble ambition of the technology industry. Instead of solving big, important challenges, the world’s smarts—and money—had been devoted to small-potatoes social-internet start-ups such as Twitter. One obvious oddity of the line—which has since been removed from the manifesto —is that Founders Fund’s most important investment at the time was Facebook, a social-network platform. But another is the idea that anyone actually wanted a flying car for real. That ambition may never have represented an actual dream. Like a jet pack, a flying car represents not just the future but the idea of individual freedom delivered through technological conquest. Taken at face value, a flying car is not an impressive dream—or at least it hasn’t been since the Wright brothers more or less attained it. Automobiles have always moved on the ground by rolling via motor. The earliest practical airplanes also rolled until they flew (and hopefully landed again). An airplane is, in a way, merely a car with wings. [ Derek Thompson: Why flying cars are an impossible dream ] In 1917, Glenn Curtiss built literally that: His Curtiss Autoplane was an automobile with detachable wings and a propeller. It never really flew effectively, but the idea persisted. Waldo Waterman’s 1937 Arrowbile was more successful at flying, though it wasn’t commercially viable. Many more actual realizations of the supposed dream of flying cars appeared in the ensuing decades. The most famous might be the Taylor Aerocar, which was certified by the federal government in 1956 but was never mass-produced. Around that time, future-oriented science-factual magazines such as Popular Mechanics frequently rehearsed the vision of the personal aircraft. By then, cars were ordinary and mainstream in America, having displaced collective transportation such as trains and streetcars. The automobile had become a more abstract kind of vehicle, one that embraced and extended personal autonomy through the power to move, without effort, anywhere else—and to do it alone. But one thing still cramped the automobile’s capacity to deliver that freedom in full: roads. Cars needed them. The open road, of which America had a seemingly endless frontier, somehow was never enough. The best way around those roads was through the air above them; as Emmett Brown told Marty McFly inside one of fiction’s most memorable flying cars, “Roads? Where we’re going, we don’t need roads.” The stifling oppression of the ground, traversed at any speed, was also an old vexation. In 1923, Hugo Gernsback—sometimes called the father of science fiction thanks to his founding Amazing Stories , an early magazine devoted to the genre—imagined a gyroscopic Helicar that would release travelers from the tyranny of New York City’s newly car-congested streets. A few years later, in 1927, Fritz Lang’s film Metropolis colonized the city’s airspace with small flying vehicles. By 1962, the children’s cartoon The Jetsons had fused those precursors with mid-century Popular Mechanics populism, making the flying car a ubiquitous commuter vehicle. Over the decades, many attempts to engineer, manufacture, and market a flying car have been undertaken, though none has succeeded. In 1973, Henry Smolinski created the AVE Mizar by attaching Cessna wings to a Ford Pinto; it killed Smolinski during a failed test flight. From the 1960s until the company went dormant in the mid-2010s, Paul Moller made numerous attempts to develop the Skycar, a personal airplane that took off and landed vertically. Around that time, Terrafugia began promising a flying car called the Transition, which remained only a few years away for years—until the company shut down in 2021. “We enter production in 2028,” Musk said of the Tesla Roadster in this week’s Texas demo, before adding, “Actually.” By all appearances, the Roadster is not a flying car of the same sort as its real and fictional precursors. The vehicle’s air-fan system seems first and principally designed to give the car’s wheels better traction on the ground, which is part of why it can go so fast—it went from zero to 60 miles per hour in less than a second during the unveiling. (Rocket thrusters attached to the back of the thing also help.) The car does not fly so much as it performs aerial acrobatics such as barrel rolls and standing jumps. Those deeds were impressive as heck. The car certainly appeared to fly, if only for a moment, in the manner of a daredevil. Whether or not it can or is intended to fly in the manner of a traveler or commuter is not yet clear. Watching the Roadster do its thing—unpiloted, to make sure the demonstration didn’t “kill anyone,” as Musk put it—I imagined wealthy gearheads wreaking havoc via ill-fated jumps and spins on suburban blocks instead of salarymen conveying themselves to work and back. [ From the November 2026 issue: Choose your overlord ] Subdued by decades of failed automobile-airplane hybrids, and perhaps exhausted by Musk’s dubious intentions, some coverage of the Tesla demo has observed , rightly, that substantial regulatory hurdles await any vehicle that leaves the road and enters airspace. But bureaucratic red tape isn’t the main reason the flying-car dream hasn’t come to pass. Rather, it’s because the dream works better as fantasy than reality. When urban modernism began to feel cramped, the skies rising above it offered the possibility of new freedom. After the continent was settled, the roads that traversed it became new prisons from which airspace might allow escape. Once the individual freedom of the automobile became universal, and the roads clogged with thousands of varmints in the rat race, the blue sky above looked like liberty. George Jetson is a cog in the proverbial machine who rises above insignificance by flying to work unfazed, where he revels in the meaninglessness of his job pressing a button to make actual machine cogs. Even Thiel’s mention of the flying car was symbolic, a paradigmatic example of the kind of dream worth dreaming, not an actual one worth waking up to. Despite the Tesla Roadster’s truly spectacular capabilities, at least as a one-off demo, it fulfills the century-old flying-car ambition on a technicality—as a vehicle for a trick driver rather than a motorist aviator. Perhaps the dream this car truly realizes is not yours or mine, but Elon Musk’s: to claim to have delivered what a century of his forebears could not.

items.title: All the Comforts of Fall
items.description: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. There’s a lot to love about fall: the changing leaves, the crisp air, the return of cozy sweaters, and, of course, pumpkin-spice everything. As the days grow shorter and the weather cools, the season offers plenty of reasons to slow down and indulge in life’s little comforts. Although fall has its familiar rituals, there are always new ways to enjoy it. Maybe you’re looking for your next great read, a recipe to try on a chilly afternoon, or an excuse to spend more time outdoors before winter arrives. To help you get into the autumn spirit, explore some of our favorite Atlantic stories and recommendations for the season. Fall Favorites Six Books to Read by the Fire Each of these titles is a perfect companion while the days grow imperceptibly longer. By Amanda Parrish Morgan Read the article. Six Movies to Get You in the Fall Mood From cozy classics to unlikely favorites, The Atlantic ’s writers and editors share their seasonal picks. By Rafaela Jinich Read the article. How Starbucks Perfected Autumn The pumpkin spice latte has defined fall for 20 years. ( From 2023 ) By Ian Bogost Read the article. Still Curious? What the falling leaves taught Thoreau : His autumnal observations held a lesson for him in his final years, Jake Lundberg writes. No one knows how big pumpkins can get . A decade ago, the world’s heaviest pumpkin weighed 2,000 pounds. Now the 3,000-pound mark is within sight, Yasmin Tayag wrote in 2024. Other Diversions Can Elizabeth Holmes drop the act? The rise of the IRL influencer What three gene-therapy deaths have in common PS Courtesy of Lynn D. My colleague Isabel Fattal recently asked readers to share a photo of something that sparks their sense of awe in the world. “We were lucky to head East before the storm because the foliage is incredibly colorful,” Lynn D. from Moretown, Vermont, shared. “This photo was taken from the Kancamagus Highway in New Hampshire.” We’ll continue to feature your responses in the coming weeks. — Rafaela

items.title: Boké : plus de 3 700 candidats au concours de recrutement des enseignants à la Fonction publique
items.description: Les épreuves du concours de recrutement des enseignants à la Fonction publique ont été officiellement lancées ce samedi 17 octobre 2026 dans la région administrative de Boké. Au total, 3 750 candidats sont répartis dans huit centres d’examen. La cérémonie de lancement s’est déroulée au complexe scolaire Collège-Lycée Filira, en présence du gouverneur de la région administrative de Boké, le général de 2e section El Hadj Aboubacar Diakité, et des représentants du ministère de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique, conduits par la cheffe de cabinet, Mme Saran Kallo. Au nom du ministre Faya François Bourouno, Mme Saran Kallo a salué l’organisation de ce concours, qu’elle inscrit dans la vision du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, visant à répondre aux attentes des enseignants et à réduire le déficit d’enseignants dans les écoles publiques. Elle s’est également réjouie du déploiement des unités de la gendarmerie pour assurer la sécurisation des épreuves des différents concours de recrutement à la Fonction publique. Prenant la parole pour donner le coup d’envoi des épreuves, le gouverneur de Boké a comparé ce concours à une compétition sportive. « Ce concours est aussi considéré comme un championnat », a-t-il déclaré, exprimant le souhait de voir un grand nombre de candidats de la région réussir les épreuves. Il a, par ailleurs, exhorté les candidats à respecter le silence et la discipline afin de faciliter le travail des surveillants et de garantir la transparence du processus. À noter que des personnes en situation de handicap prennent également part à ce concours, qui se déroule dans un climat décrit comme serein dans la région de Boké. Mamadouba Camara, Boké L’article Boké : plus de 3 700 candidats au concours de recrutement des enseignants à la Fonction publique est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump
items.description: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine. The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump’s support slumped. The Lindsey Graham Act — named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill — had allowed Trump the authority to impose duties up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. The legislation, which Trump signed into law last month, targeted Russia’s energy and defence sectors, President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials, as well as Moscow’s so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to circumvent Western sanctions. Trump’s reversal on the Russia sanctions comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel into global markets. The US president’s war in Iran has sparked crippling oil shortages and price spikes, creating major headwinds for his Republican Party ahead of midterm elections next month. Asked if he was being made a scapegoat for Trump’s domestic woes ahead of the vote, Zelensky just smiled . “This is my answer,” he told journalists in Brussels, after an extended pause. In another sign of strained relations between the United States and Ukraine, Trump branded Kyiv’s actions a “disgrace” after Zelensky ordered his forces to resume strikes on Russian refineries. “I defend the interests of Ukraine and the Ukrainian people exclusively,” Zelensky said after talks with EU leaders. The breakdown between Trump and Zelensky has fuelled fears that the US leader is siding with Moscow. Those concerns have been heightened by disruptions to a critical US-provided satellite system that has hampered Ukraine’s ability to counter Russia’s intense bombardments. Ukraine uses technology from Elon Musk’s SpaceX for battlefield communications, but the tech billionaire — a virulent Zelensky critic — said his company was not behind the disruption, while a US official denied any intervention by Trump. ‘Increase pressure’ European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky as he grappled with Trump. “This is no time to withdraw the support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia’s sanctions,” European Council chief Antonio Costa said. “Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure.” Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said that “the situation in Ukraine is currently truly dire, with numerous Russian attacks and a tense relationship between Ukraine and the US.” “It is crucial that we, as Europe, demonstrate our unconditional support for them today — and explore what additional steps we can take,” he said. Zelensky asked the bloc — Ukraine’s biggest international backer — to provide more Patriot missiles to shoot down Russian missiles and come up with an extra 70 billion euros ($79 billion) in support next year to help Kyiv keep fighting. Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defences ahead of winter, when temperatures can plummet to as low as -20°C and Moscow’s attacks threaten electricity, heating and water systems. Russian strikes on the southern cities of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia killed a 64-year-old man and at least 17 people, including an 11-year-old girl, Ukrainian authorities said Saturday. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen confirmed that Zelensky’s 70-billion euro plea “has to be covered” and urged partner countries to “step in” and help. French President Emmanuel Macron said Kyiv’s backers will analyse the demand, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the European Union will discuss it before the end of the year. The EU is currently paying out instalments of a 90-billion-euro loan for Kyiv that was set to help cover funding to the end of 2027. But Ukrainian authorities have warned they will still face a major budget black hole as Russian strikes have battered the country’s economy. The talks on new funding have reignited calls for the EU to tap around 200 billion euros in frozen Russian central bank assets to fund Ukraine. “The frozen assets are there. That’s what should be used for supporting Ukraine,” said Latvian premier Andris Kulbergs. But there seems little momentum on that front as Belgium, where most of the funds are held, remains opposed.

items.title: Egypt's President Sisi pledges to leave office when term ends in 2030
items.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that he would not seek to remain in office when his current term expires in 2030, describing the matter as “completely settled”. Sisi, 71, a former army general who became president in 2014, made the remarks at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy in the New Administrative Capital, one of his flagship megaprojects. Speaking to graduates and state officials in the sprawling new city east of Cairo, Sisi said the Egyptian constitution “would not be touched”. “The period leading up to 2030 will be the end of my term as president of the state, if I am still alive. This is completely settled and there will be no discussion about it,” he said. The Egyptian constitution, approved in 2014 following the 2013 military ouster of late president Mohamed Morsi, originally limited presidents to two four-year terms. Constitutional amendments approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six years and included transitional provisions that allowed Sisi to run for an additional term. Under those amendments, Sisi was re-elected in 2023 for a six-year term that is due to expire in 2030. Critics and opposition figures have speculated about the possibility of further constitutional changes that could allow him to remain in office beyond 2030. Before running for president, Sisi denied having political ambitions, but he resigned from his position as defence minister in 2014 and entered the race he went on to win. On Saturday, he said the run-up to 2030 would be used to groom a new generation of leaders, with the Military Academy training hundreds of prospective officials, ministers and presidential candidates in statecraft and leadership. During his 12 years in power, Sisi has overseen an ambitious state-led development programme centred on megaprojects which critics say have relied heavily on borrowing and contributed to Egypt’s mounting debt burden and economic pressures. Sisi’s presidency has also faced sustained criticism from international human rights organisations over restrictions on political opposition, civil society and freedom of expression , allegations the government rejects, saying its policies are necessary to preserve stability and security.

items.title: Le ténor tunisien Hassen Doss distingué à Rome
items.description: Le ténor tunisien Hassen Doss a reçu, à Rome, le Prix international d’Excellence Euro-Méditerranéen 2026 — également connu sous le nom d’«Oscar de la Méditerranée» — pour son parcours artistique et sa contribution à la promotion de la culture, de la coopération et du dialogue entre les peuples des deux rives de la Méditerranée. La distinction a été remise le 14 octobre, lors de la quatrième édition de cet événement, qui s’est tenu dans la salle Giovanni Spadolini du ministère italien de la Culture. La cérémonie a réuni des représentants de l’ambassade de Tunisie en Italie, des diplomates, des responsables institutionnels ainsi que des personnalités issues des milieux universitaires, culturels et médiatiques. Le prix a été remis au chanteur lyrique tunisien par Dündar Kesapli, président de l’Association des journalistes de la Méditerranée, à l'origine de cette initiative visant à mettre à l’honneur des personnalités s’étant distinguées dans les domaines de la culture, de l’art, de la diplomatie, des médias, du sport ou de l’engagement social. « Je suis profondément ému» , a déclaré Hassen Doss à l’agence Tap, soulignant la portée symbolique de recevoir une telle distinction en Italie — pays doté d’une immense tradition lyrique — aux côtés de personnalités internationales, telles que l’ancien capitaine de l'AS Rome, Francesco Totti. Le ténor a qualifié ce prix d’aboutissement d’un long cheminement marqué par l’engagement, la persévérance et le travail. Formé à l’Institut de musique de Sousse et à l’Institut supérieur de musique de Tunis, Hassen Doss est considéré comme l’un des pionniers de la diffusion du chant lyrique en Tunisie. Au cours de sa carrière, il a contribué à rapprocher le public tunisien de l’opéra, en proposant une fusion originale entre technique vocale lyrique, tradition musicale arabe et sonorités contemporaines. Parmi ses expériences les plus marquantes, on peut citer ses participations au Festival international de Carthage, en 2018 et 2022, ainsi que sa contribution aux versions tunisiennes de ‘‘Carmen’’ de Georges Bizet et de ‘‘ La Traviata’’ de Giuseppe Verdi. Son répertoire comprend par ailleurs des airs d’opéra, des chansons italiennes et napolitaines, ainsi que des compositions originales en dialecte tunisien. L’article Le ténor tunisien Hassen Doss distingué à Rome est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: En Azerbaïdjan, l’interdiction du voile à l’école suscite des tensions
items.description: L’affaire fait grand bruit dans certains pays musulmans et suscite des grincements de dents jusque chez certains dirigeants. En Azerbaïdjan, ancienne république soviétique à majorité musulmane, le voile islamique n’est visiblement pas le bienvenu à l’école. En vertu d’une décision des autorités datée du 21 septembre dernier, les élèves et les enseignants sont sommés de se conformer à l’uniforme scolaire. Selon Courrier international , les autorités azerbaïdjanaises interdisent depuis quelques semaines les vêtements « qui rompent l’uniformité de l’uniforme scolaire imposé ou qui ne sont pas conformes au principe de la laïcité ». Résultat : des manifestations ont éclaté dans plusieurs endroits du pays, notamment à Bakou, la capitale, ainsi que dans certains quartiers de la périphérie de la capitale. Il y a quelques jours, les contrôles vestimentaires dans les établissements scolaires ont dégénéré en affrontements avec la police. Des manifestants ont tenté d’incendier des véhicules et des bâtiments, selon des informations parcellaires qui filtrent de ce pays fermé et repris par les médias étrangers. Plusieurs personnes ont été arrêtées. Interdiction du voile à l’école en Azerbaïdjan : une décision qui fait désordre Le lendemain, de nouveaux affrontements ont été signalés autour de certaines écoles alors que des poursuites pénales pour troubles à l’ordre public ont été engagées contre plusieurs dizaines de manifestants, selon ces sources. La polémique a pris de l’ampleur après la diffusion d’une vidéo montrant deux écolières en pleurs, auxquelles l’accès à leur établissement a été refusé en raison de leur voile, d’après plusieurs médias. Cette interdiction, justifiée par les autorités au nom de la laïcité, suscite d’autant plus de réactions que l’Azerbaïdjan est un pays où plus de 97 % de la population est musulmane. La controverse a rapidement franchi les frontières, suscitant la réaction notamment du voisin turc, pourtant l’un des principaux alliés de Bakou. Le président turc Recep Tayyip Erdogan a vivement critiqué les restrictions visant le port du voile dans les établissements scolaires azerbaïdjanais. Lors d’un discours prononcé aux Nations unies le 22 septembre, il avait dénoncé « les interdictions du voile mises en place dans les écoles de certains pays, qui sont une atteinte aux droits les plus fondamentaux ». Même si le dirigeant turc ne cite pas expressément les autorités azerbaïdjanaises, il reste que l’allusion ne souffre d’aucune équivoque. Signe de tension : le 3 octobre, des manifestants s’étaient rassemblés devant le consulat azerbaïdjanais à Istanbul pour protester contre cette décision. « Notre voile n’est pas un uniforme scolaire. Il ne s’agit même pas simplement d’une question de droits humains. Le voile constitue l’identité même de la femme musulmane », a déclaré une organisatrice du rassemblement dont les propos ont été repris par les médias. Une mobilisation qui illustre les tensions qu’engendrent souvent ce genre de décisions qui touchent à la fois à la liberté religieuse et à la place de l’islam dans l’espace public, sujets encore très sensibles, voire tabous, particulièrement dans les sociétés musulmanes. Le voile, un sujet qui divise au-delà de l’Azerbaïdjan Le problème divise parfois même les sociétés occidentales où la laïcité est profondément ancrée dans les mœurs politiques. En France, par exemple, le port de signes religieux ostensibles par les élèves dans les établissements scolaires publics est interdit depuis la loi de 2004. Mais la question du voile continue d’alimenter les tensions politiques, notamment autour des propositions de l’extrême droite visant à étendre les interdictions à d’autres espaces de la vie publique. En Suisse également, le port du voile fait régulièrement l’objet de débats politiques et juridiques, même si les règles varient selon les situations et les institutions concernées. Face au tollé soulevé par la décision, les autorités azerbaïdjanaises vont-elles lâcher du lest ? Pas sûr compte tenu de la nature du régime. Le 4 octobre dernier, le chef de l’État, Ilham Aliev a adressé un avertissement à ceux qui contestent les choix de son pays : « Qu’ils ne se mêlent pas de nos affaires, qu’ils ne mettent pas leur nez dans notre mode de vie et qu’ils ne nous disent pas ce que nous devons faire ». Ilham Aliev est au pouvoir depuis 2003. L’article En Azerbaïdjan, l’interdiction du voile à l’école suscite des tensions est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: ‘Tilting the balance’ explanation for Afi Agbenyo’s EC appointment deeply troubling – Victoria Bright
items.description: International corporate lawyer Victoria Bright has described the explanation that Afi Agbenyo’s appointment as Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC) was intended to “tilt the balance” as deeply troubling, warning that it could undermine public confidence in the Commission’s independence. She said the justification appeared inconsistent with President John Mahama’s assurance that the new EC leadership must act impartially and must not favour his government or the National Democratic Congress (NDC). Speaking on JoyNews ’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, Ms Bright welcomed President Mahama’s call for the new EC leadership to remain neutral but said the assurance could be undermined by statements suggesting that political balance influenced the appointments. She said that the government needed to communicate its position consistently to avoid creating doubts about the Commission’s independence. “The President’s instruction that neither his government nor his party should receive preferential treatment is very welcome,” she said. “But government must speak consistently because an assurance of neutrality sits uneasily alongside an explanation based on tilting parties and balance.” During the discussion, Ms Bright was asked whether the explanation had created an unnecessary problem for the President, given that Ms Agbenyo’s professional background, including her work with the German development agency GIZ, had been cited as evidence of her capacity to act impartially. In response, she clarified that she was not accusing the President of creating a problem but was concerned about the mixed messages surrounding the appointment. “I’m not saying that the President has caused any problems. What I’m saying, I did say that his comments were very welcome.” “His comments on impartiality, the need for all our commissioners, including these two appointees, to be impartial, those comments are very welcome,” she said. “But I’m saying that you can’t have that on the one hand and then on the other hand, you get an explanation saying, ‘Oh, but we have to tilt the political balance.’ Which suggests that there’s some political influence.” Ms Bright said the government needed to be careful about how it explained appointments to institutions expected to operate independently of political parties. Ms Bright said the government risked repeating the very problem it had previously criticised if political considerations were used to influence appointments to an independent institution. “If government believes that previous appointments weakened the EC’s independence, it should strengthen the safeguards that protect independent judgement,” she said. “Because, for me, appointments intended to adjust partisan influence will now be risking and entrenching the very problem that the government previously condemned.” Ms Bright said such an explanation placed an unnecessary burden on the new appointees, as it could lead the public to judge their decisions through the lens of an alleged political motive. “We need to defer to these appointees because this kind of explanation places an unnecessary burden on them,” she said. “Even if Miss Agbenyo is determined to act impartially, government has now supplied the political purpose against which people may judge their decisions.” Council of State’s role The corporate lawyer also called for greater attention to the role of the Council of State in the appointment process, stressing that its advisory function formed an important part of the constitutional arrangements. She said the public needed clarity on the criteria used to assess candidates, including whether their recent political activities had been disclosed and considered. “I think the Council of State must also feature in this discussion, to be honest, because its advisory role is an important part of the constitutional process,” she said. “What criteria were used? And were recent campaign roles disclosed and evaluated? How were concerns about public confidence addressed?” Ms Bright, however, was careful not to suggest that the appointment process had breached any constitutional or procedural requirement. She acknowledged that she was not privy to the Council of State’s deliberations or records and could not determine what considerations informed its advice. “I don’t know what criteria they used. I don’t know whether concerns about public confidence were addressed. And I’m not even suggesting that we’ve established any procedural breach,” she said. Her concern, she explained, was that the explanation offered for the appointments could affect how the public viewed the Commission, regardless of whether the process followed the required procedures. “All I’m saying is that the public, the optics don’t look good,” she added. EC appointment process must improve Ms Bright urged the government and relevant institutions to use the controversy as an opportunity to improve the process for appointing members of the Electoral Commission. She said publishing clear selection criteria could help reduce political disputes and improve public understanding of how candidates were assessed. According to her, greater transparency would help address concerns about political affiliations and ensure that appointments were judged against established standards rather than competing political claims. “We should use this recurring controversy to improve the appointment process,” she said. “Maybe the criteria should be published in future to stop all this.”

items.description: Le ministre de l'Énergie et du Pétrole de la République islamique de Mauritanie, Mohamed Abdel Vetah, a été reçu vendredi par le chef de l'État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, dans le cadre de la politique de souveraineté énergétique que conduit le président de la République du Sénégal. Le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a reçu en audience le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, Mohamed Abdel Vetah, ministre de l'Énergie et du Pétrole de la République islamique de Mauritanie, ancien Haut-Commissaire de l'Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS). « Cette audience s'inscrit dans la politique de souveraineté énergétique que conduit le chef de l'État. Du fleuve Sénégal, dont l'OMVS valorise l'eau et l'énergie, au gisement gazier Grand Tortue Ahmeyim que partagent les deux pays, Dakar et Nouakchott construisent ensemble une part décisive de leur avenir énergétique », renseigne une note de la présidence publiée samedi. A lire aussi : Production Sangomar et GTA : 2,94 millions de barils et 0,33 million de mètres cubes de GNL produits D’après la même source, l'arrivée à la tête du ministère mauritanien de l'Énergie d'un acteur qui connaît intimement cette coopération ouvre de nouvelles perspectives à ce partenariat de bon voisinage. Ainsi, Mohamed Abdel Vetah a remercié les autorités sénégalaises pour l'accompagnement dont il a bénéficié durant près de quatre ans à la tête de l'OMVS, dont le siège est à Dakar. Dans ses nouvelles fonctions, il entend poursuivre cet engagement au service des populations du Sénégal et de la Mauritanie. M. DIEME

items.title: Les exportations alimentaires de la Tunisie augmentent de 19,9 % (9 mois de 2026)
items.description: La balance commerciale alimentaire de la Tunisie a enregistré, au cours des neuf premiers mois de l’année 2026, un excédent de 919,8 millions de dinars. Le taux de couverture des importations par les exportations a atteint 116,3 %, tandis que la valeur des exportations alimentaires a progressé de 19,9 % par rapport à la même période de l'année 2025. À fin septembre 2026, l'huile d'olive représentait 61 % et les dattes 9,4 % de la valeur totale des exportations alimentaires. C’est ce qu’a indiqué le ministre du Commerce et du Développement des exportations, Samir Abid, lors d’une journée d’information organisée par son département en collaboration avec le Conseil bancaire et financier (CBF), le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, à Tunis, et qui visait à faire connaître les mécanismes et les facilités financières et bancaires disponibles pour financer les activités de transformation, de promotion et d’exportation de ces deux produits phares de l’agriculture tunisienne. Selon Diwan FM , le ministre a souligné la nécessité de renforcer le financement des exportations d’huile d’olive et de dattes, et de développer le partenariat entre le secteur bancaire et financier et les entreprises exportatrices de ces deux filières exportatrices. Le but étant de soutenir la compétitivité des produits tunisiens et d’accroître leur valeur ajoutée sur les marchés mondiaux. Concernant la campagne 2025-2026, M. Abid a indiqué que les exportations d’huile d’olive ont dépassé 399 400 tonnes durant la période allant de novembre 2025 à octobre 2026, pour une valeur avoisinant les 5,016 milliards de dinars. Cela représente une hausse de 48,7 % en volume et de 39,4 % en valeur par rapport à la campagne précédente. Par ailleurs, l’huile d’olive extra vierge a constitué environ 90 % des quantités exportées, tandis que la part de l’huile conditionnée n’a pas excédé 15 %. Tunisie | Mesures pour impulser les exportations d’huile d’olive et de dattes Quant aux exportations de dattes, elles ont franchi pour la première fois la barre du milliard de dinars, atteignant 1,011 milliard de dinars, contre 882,7 millions de dinars lors de la campagne précédente ; les quantités exportées ont, quant à elles, progressé pour atteindre 159 400 tonnes, contre 138 300 tonnes auparavant. Actuellement, les dattes tunisiennes sont exportées vers environ 86 pays à travers les différents continents. M. Abid a souligné l’importance de fournir des financements adaptés aux différentes étapes de l’activité — de la production et la transformation au stockage, au conditionnement et à la commercialisation —, en particulier au profit des petites et moyennes entreprises (PME). Il a également insisté sur le développement de mécanismes d’assurance des exportations et de couverture contre les risques de change. Par ailleurs, il a réaffirmé la nécessité de poursuivre les efforts visant à diversifier les marchés extérieurs, à renforcer la promotion des produits tunisiens et à développer les exportations d’huile d’olive conditionnée ainsi que de produits à haute valeur ajoutée. Il a enfin préconisé une révision des interventions du Fonds de promotion des exportations (Foprodex), afin d’améliorer l'efficacité du soutien accordé aux entreprises. I. B. items.title: Décès du journaliste Gamal Nkrumah, fils de Kwame Nkrumah
items.description: Le journaliste Gamal Nkrumah, fils de Kwame Nkrumah, figure historique de l’indépendance du Ghana, est décédé, le 15 octobre 2026, au Caire en Egypte de suite de maladie. La figure d’Al-Ahram Weekly, Gamal Nkrumah, fils de Kwame Nkrumah, décédé ce jeudi 15 octobre 2026 au Caire de suite d’une longue maladie. En tant que journaliste, il s’était imposé comme l’un des spécialistes des affaires du continent africain. Selon sa famille, dans un communiqué, Gamal est un «homme d’une profonde curiosité intellectuelle, indépendant d’esprit et animé de convictions discrètes mais fermes». Il «a perpétué, à sa manière, l’héritage durable de notre père, tout en construisant une vie et une réputation solidement ancrées dans ses propres principes et réalisations», a poursuivi sa famille. Quant à la rédaction d’Al-Ahram Weekly, elle a salué la mémoire d’«un ami et un collègue cher, dont les analyses ont enrichi les pages du journal pendant plusieurs décennies». Pour elle, Gamal est caractérisé par sa «douceur, son humour et sa présence chaleureuse». Sur X, le ministre égyptien des Affaires étrangères, Badr Abdelatty, a exprimé «sa profonde tristesse à la suite du décès de Gamal Nkrumah, fils du dirigeant africain Kwame Nkrumah, prénommé en hommage à Gamal Abdel Nasser». Par Wakat Séra L’article Décès du journaliste Gamal Nkrumah, fils de Kwame Nkrumah est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Top 5 African countries with the most visa-free travel if you own their passport
items.description: African passports differ significantly in the number of destinations their holders can visit without obtaining a visa before departure, with Seychelles, Mauritius and South Africa leading the continent in international travel access. The Henley Passport Index, which uses data from the International Air Transport Association (IATA), ranks passports according to the number of destinations their holders can access without a prior visa. Its 2026 rankings place Seychelles among Africa’s strongest passports, followed by Mauritius and South Africa. Based on the 2026 rankings and available passport-mobility data, here are five African countries whose passports offer extensive international travel access. Seychelles Seychelles has one of Africa’s most powerful passports, giving its citizens broad access to destinations across the world without securing a visa in advance. The island nation retained its position as Africa’s leading passport in the 2026 Henley Passport Index, ranking among the top 25 passports globally in the July update. According to the Seychelles News Agency, the passport provided visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 155 destinations at that time. Its international mobility gives Seychellois citizens greater flexibility when planning holidays, business trips and other short-term journeys abroad. The country’s position reflects the benefits of its international relations and the travel arrangements it has established with other countries. Mauritius Mauritius ranks among Africa’s strongest passports, offering its citizens extensive travel opportunities across several regions. The country has consistently placed near the top of continental passport rankings, with access to numerous destinations in Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and other parts of the world. Mauritian citizens benefit from visa-free arrangements and visa-on-arrival facilities in a range of countries, making international travel more convenient for tourism and business. Its strong passport position also reflects Mauritius’s international engagement and the agreements that facilitate movement between its citizens and other countries. South Africa South Africa ranks third among Africa’s strongest passports in the 2026 rankings, providing its citizens with substantial international travel access. South African passport holders can visit a range of destinations without obtaining a visa beforehand, although entry conditions differ by country. The passport is particularly useful for regional travel within Africa, while also providing access to destinations in parts of Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean. Despite its relatively strong position on the continent, South African citizens still require visas for several major destinations, depending on the purpose and length of their visit. Botswana Botswana is among the African countries whose passports offer comparatively broad international travel access. Its passport provides entry to a range of countries without a prior visa, including destinations within Africa and selected countries beyond the continent. Botswana’s position places it among the leading African passports after Seychelles, Mauritius and South Africa in several 2026 passport-mobility comparisons. For Botswana citizens, these arrangements can reduce the paperwork and planning required for international holidays, visits and some business trips. Namibia Namibia rounds out the five African countries with strong passport mobility in several 2026 rankings. Namibian passport holders enjoy visa-free access to a number of destinations, alongside access to other countries through visa-on-arrival arrangements. The passport offers opportunities for regional travel in southern Africa and entry to selected destinations elsewhere in the world. Although Namibia does not provide the same level of access as Seychelles or Mauritius, it remains among the African countries whose citizens enjoy comparatively broad international mobility. items.title: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde A former spokesperson to ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande has dismissed claims by Babachir Lawal that former President Muhammadu Buhari considered Osinbajo’s 2023 presidential ambition “highly immoral and distasteful”. Akande, who served as Osinbajo’s spokesperson from 2015 to 2023, described the allegation as false in a statement on Saturday, saying Buhari had personally offered to support the former vice-president’s ambition on at least four occasions. Osinbajo contested the All Progressives Congress presidential primary in 2022 but lost to Bola Tinubu, who went on to win the 2023 presidential election. Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, ADC, and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, had alleged in a recent interview that Buhari would have found it difficult to support Osinbajo’s ambition because of his longstanding relationship with Tinubu, a former Lagos State governor. Reacting, Akande said he had watched the interview in which Lawal made allegations against Osinbajo and chose to respond because he was present when decisions concerning the former vice-president’s office were taken. He said Buhari had, on at least four separate occasions, personally offered to support Osinbajo, asking him, “If I don’t support you, who will I support?” “He was consistent. During the APC presidential primaries in 2022, while campaigns were underway, President Buhari openly commended Vice President Osinbajo at a Federal Executive Council meeting for the dignified, issues-based manner in which he was conducting his campaign across the country. He spoke in a laudatory tone. The entire Council witnessed it.” “That is not a President who found Osinbajo’s ambition distasteful. That is a President who broached it, encouraged and applauded it,” Akande added. Osinbajo contested the APC presidential primary in June 2022, finishing third with 235 votes, behind now president Bola Tinubu, who won with 1,271 votes, and Rotimi Amaechi, who scored 316. items.title: Partenariat commune de Tambacounda–Swami Agrisa : 7 milliards de FCfa pour une huilerie et des infrastructures de stockage
items.description: La mairie de Tambacounda et Swami Agrisau, filiale de Senegindia Sa, ont signé, le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, une convention de sept milliards de FCfa pour la construction d’une huilerie, d’une centrale solaire, d’un magasin de stockage d’oignons et de pommes de terre et d’un parking pour gros porteurs. Le projet devrait générer entre 500 et 800 emplois directs. TAMBACOUNDA – Un important projet agro-industriel sera mis en place dans la commune de Tambacounda. D’un coût global de sept milliards de FCfa, selon le directeur général de Swami Agrisau, Hithesh Gorasia, l’investissement prévoit la construction d’une huilerie, d’une centrale solaire, d’un magasin de stockage de 20 000 tonnes d’oignon et de pomme de terre, ainsi que d’un parking pour gros porteurs de 10 hectares. Avec ce projet, le responsable de la société annonce la création, dans un premier temps, entre 500 et 800 emplois directs et plusieurs autres indirects. « Les populations de Tambacounda ont toujours plaidé pour une deuxième usine capable d’absorber une partie du chômage dans la commune. Nous pensons qu’avec ce projet, ce sera le cas », a déclaré le maire de la commune, Papa Banda Dièye. Le projet devrait également améliorer la circulation urbaine grâce à un parking destiné aux gros porteurs, qui va contribuer à réduire le stationnement anarchique et les risques d’accidents. Quant au magasin de stockage, il permettra de limiter les pertes post-récolte et d’offrir de meilleures conditions de conservation aux producteurs. L’huilerie, d’une capacité de transformation de 60 tonnes d’arachide, va faciliter l’écoulement de la production locale. « Nous allons y stocker d’abord une partie de notre production provenant de la zone des Niayes, en attendant d’accompagner les producteurs locaux et de vulgariser la culture de l’oignon et de la pomme de terre dans la localité », a expliqué le Dg de Swami Agrisau. Le projet s’étendra sur 25 hectares répartis entre l’usine (10 ha), le parking (10 ha) et la centrale solaire (5 ha). Le démarrage des travaux reste toutefois suspendu à l’obtention des autorisations administratives. « Dès que nous les aurons obtenues, les travaux commenceront », a assuré Hithesh Gorasia. La réception des infrastructures est prévue en janvier 2028. Les travaux seront réalisés avec la participation de la main-d’œuvre locale. Boubacar Agna CAMARA (Correspondant)

items.title: ECOWAS donates $250,000 to support Ghana’s June 29 flood victims
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has announced a $250,000 relief contribution from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to support victims of the June floods in Ghana. The amount, equivalent to approximately GH¢3 million, has been transferred to the Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA), which will oversee the distribution of the assistance to affected persons. In a Facebook post on Friday, October 16, Mr Ablakwa said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) had agreed to engage ADRA as an independent implementing partner for the relief intervention. He explained that the decision was intended to ensure an independent process for identifying beneficiaries and distributing the funds, with the government not directly involved in selecting those who would receive assistance. The announcement was made during the inauguration of Ghana’s National Consultative Committee on Regional Integration (NCCRI), which is mandated to oversee the implementation of ECOWAS regional integration programmes and social interventions in the country. Mr Ablakwa also emphasised the need for transparency and accountability in managing the donation, indicating that the distribution process would be guided by integrity. The ECOWAS contribution is expected to provide relief to people whose homes and livelihoods were affected by the June floods, as the government and humanitarian organisations continue efforts to address the consequences of the disaster. The floods, which occurred on June 29, affected more than 38,000 people across the Greater Accra Region, displaced over 7,700 households and claimed at least 15 lives. The relief package adds to ongoing efforts to support affected communities as they recover from the damage caused by the flooding.

items.title: Préscolaire et décrochage, les dossiers qui attendent Kamal Hachoumi
items.description: Nommé ministre délégué chargé du Préscolaire et de la Lutte contre le décrochage scolaire, Kamal Hachoumi hérite de deux chantiers majeurs pour l’école publique. Généralisation de l’enseignement préscolaire, amélioration des conditions des éducateurs et éducatrices, prévention des abandons scolaires : les engagements électoraux de l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) constituent une première feuille de route pour le nouveau responsable. La nouvelle architecture gouvernementale confie à Kamal Hachoumi la responsabilité de deux dossiers étroitement liés à l’égalité des chances : le développement de l’enseignement préscolaire et la lutte contre le décrochage scolaire. Universitaire spécialisé en sciences politiques et en droit constitutionnel, membre du bureau politique de l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP), le nouveau ministre délégué devra contribuer à la mise en œuvre des orientations éducatives du gouvernement dirigé par Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri. Son parcours l’a conduit à occuper plusieurs fonctions administratives et universitaires. Il a notamment assuré, entre août 2022 et août 2023, les fonctions de secrétaire général par intérim du ministère de l’Inclusion économique, de la Petite Entreprise et de l’Emploi. Il a également été directeur des ressources humaines au sein de ce département, de mars 2022 à octobre 2023, et vice-doyen de la Faculté des sciences juridiques, économiques et sociales d’Aïn Sebaâ entre septembre 2016 et juillet 2017. Professeur universitaire et coordinateur d’un master en études politiques et institutionnelles approfondies à la Faculté de droit d’Agdal, à Rabat, Kamal Hachoumi a aussi travaillé comme expert-consultant senior auprès du Nordic Centre for Conflict Transformation, basé à Stockholm. Le statut des éducateurs du préscolaire au cœur des attentes Parmi les dossiers qui attendent le nouveau responsable figure la poursuite de la généralisation de l’offre préscolaire. L’objectif ne consiste pas seulement à élargir l’accès à cette étape de la scolarisation, mais aussi à garantir la qualité de l’encadrement et des apprentissages proposés aux enfants. La situation des éducatrices et éducateurs du préscolaire constitue un autre enjeu. Ces professionnels réclament une amélioration de leurs conditions sociales, économiques et administratives. La question de leur statut, de leur rémunération et de leur formation reste donc centrale pour assurer la stabilité des équipes et la qualité de l’enseignement dispensé aux plus jeunes. Le programme électoral de l’USFP prévoit de généraliser un enseignement préscolaire gratuit et de qualité pour tous les enfants à partir de quatre ans. Le parti s’engage également à construire et à équiper des unités préscolaires dans l’ensemble des communes rurales et des quartiers insuffisamment équipés. Il préconise, en parallèle, la formation et la qualification des éducatrices et éducateurs selon des normes nationales unifiées. Ces mesures supposent de mobiliser des moyens humains et matériels suffisants, mais aussi de veiller à ce que l’extension de l’offre ne se fasse pas au détriment de la qualité. Prévenir le décrochage avant la rupture scolaire Le second volet du portefeuille confié à Hachoumi concerne la lutte contre le décrochage scolaire. L’USFP propose de renforcer les dispositifs de détection précoce des élèves exposés au risque d’abandon, afin d’intervenir avant que les difficultés scolaires ou sociales ne conduisent à une rupture définitive avec l’école. Le programme prévoit également d’élargir les aides sociales destinées aux familles défavorisées, notamment dans les zones rurales et périurbaines. Les bourses, le transport scolaire, la restauration et l’hébergement figurent parmi les leviers identifiés pour réduire les obstacles matériels à la poursuite de la scolarité. Le parti entend aussi développer les écoles de la deuxième chance et les programmes de réintégration pour les jeunes ayant quitté le système scolaire. Il propose enfin de renforcer le soutien pédagogique gratuit pour les élèves confrontés à des difficultés d’apprentissage. Ces engagements appellent une action coordonnée entre les établissements, les familles et les services chargés de l’accompagnement social. Le repérage des élèves en difficulté ne peut produire de résultats sans solutions adaptées à leurs besoins, qu’il s’agisse de soutien scolaire, de transport ou d’aide aux familles. Des engagements électoraux à traduire en mesures concrètes Dans son programme, l’USFP présente l’école publique comme un levier de justice sociale et d’égalité des chances. Le parti défend une réforme éducative destinée à restaurer la confiance dans l’enseignement public, à favoriser l’apprentissage et la citoyenneté et à préparer les élèves aux évolutions de l’économie et de la société. La réhabilitation des établissements, leur équipement en laboratoires et en bibliothèques, ainsi que le développement des espaces sportifs et culturels font également partie des engagements annoncés. Pour Kamal Hachoumi, l’enjeu sera de traduire ces orientations en actions concrètes, avec des objectifs mesurables et un calendrier d’exécution. La généralisation du préscolaire, l’amélioration des conditions de travail des éducateurs et la prévention du décrochage constitueront des indicateurs importants pour évaluer les premières avancées de son département.
